title: Esther 1:13
text: And the king said to the wise men who knew the times (for so [was] the king's manner toward all who knew law and judgment;

title: Esther 1:14
text: and the next to him were Carshena, Shethar, Admatha, Tarshish, Meres, Marsena, Memucan, the seven princes of Persia and Media who saw the king's face, who sat first in the kingdom),

title: Esther 1:15
text: What shall we do with queen Vashti according to law, because she has not done the command of the king Ahasuerus by the eunuchs?

title: Esther 1:16
text: And Memucan answered before the king and princes, Vashti the queen has not only done wrong to the king, but also to all the princes, and to all the people who [are] in all the provinces of king Ahasuerus.

title: Esther 1:17
text: For the matter of the queen shall go out to all women, so that their husbands shall be despised in their eyes, and it shall be reported that king Ahasuerus commanded to bring Vashti the queen in before him, but she did not come.

title: Esther 1:18
text: And this day the princesses of Persia and Media shall say the same to all the king's princes who have heard of the deed of the queen. And there [will be] contempt and strife.

title: Esther 1:19
text: If it please the king, let there be a royal command from him, and let it be written among the laws of the Persians and the Medes, so that it may not be changed, that Vashti come no more before king Ahasuerus. And let the king give her royal state to another who is better than she is.

title: Esther 1:20
text: And when the king's decree which he shall make shall be published throughout all his empire (for it is great), all the wives shall give their husbands honor, both the great and small.

title: Esther 1:21
text: And the saying pleased the king and the princes. And the king did according to the word of Memucan.

title: Esther 1:22
text: For he sent letters into all the king's provinces, into every province according to the writing of it, and to every people in their language, so that every man should bear rule in his own house, and published according to the language of every people.

title: Esther 2:1
text: After these things, when the wrath of king Ahasuerus had calmed down, he remembered Vashti and what she had done, and what was decreed against her.

title: Esther 2:2
text: And the king's servants who served him said, Let beautiful young virgins be sought for the king.

title: Esther 2:3
text: And let the king choose officers in all the provinces of his kingdom, so that they may gather together all the beautiful young virgins to Shushan the palace, to the house of the women, to the hand of Hegai the king's eunuch, keeper of the women. And let their ointments be given.

title: Esther 2:4
text: And let the young woman who pleases the king be queen instead of Vashti. And the thing pleased the king, and he did so.

title: Esther 2:5
text: In Shushan the palace there was a certain Jew whose name [was] Mordecai, the son of Jair, the son of Shimei, the son of Kish, a Benjamite

title: Esther 2:6
text: who had been carried away from Jerusalem with the captivity which had been carried away with Jeconiah king of Judah, whom Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon had carried away.

title: Esther 2:7
text: And he brought up Hadassah, that [is], Esther, his uncle's daughter. For she had neither father nor mother, and the young woman [was] fair and beautiful, whom Mordecai, when her father and mother were dead, took for his own daughter.

title: Esther 2:8
text: And it happened when the king's command and his order was heard, and when many young women had been gathered to Shushan the palace, into the hand of Hegai, Esther was also brought to the king's house, into the hand of Hegai, keeper of the women.

title: Esther 2:9
text: And the young woman pleased him, and she received kindness from him. And he quickly gave to her purifiers and her portion. And seven young women [who were] fit to be given her, out of the king's house. And he moved her and her servant women to the best place in the house of the women.

title: Esther 2:10
text: Esther had not revealed her people nor her kindred, for Mordecai had commanded her that she should not show [it].

title: Esther 2:11
text: And Mordecai walked every day in front of the court of the women's house in order to know how Esther did and what was to become of her.

title: Esther 2:12
text: And when the turn of each young woman had come to go in to king Ahasuerus, after she had been purified twelve months, according to the law of the women (for so the days of their anointing were done, six months with oil of myrrh, and six months with sweet odors, and with the perfumes of the women).

title: Esther 2:13
text: And in this way the young woman came to the king. Whatever she desired was given her to go with her out of the house of the women to the king's house.

title: Esther 2:14
text: She went in the evening, and on the next day she returned to the second house of the women, into the hand of Shaashgaz, the king's officer who kept the concubines. She did not come in to the king any more, unless the king delighted in her, and she was called by name.

title: Esther 2:15
text: And when the turn of Esther, the daughter of Abihail the uncle of Mordecai who had taken her for his daughter, had come to go in to the king, she asked nothing but what was chosen by Hegai the king's officer, the keeper of the women. And Esther had favor in the sight of all who looked on her.

title: Esther 2:16
text: And Esther was taken to king Ahasuerus into his royal house in the tenth month, which [is] the month Tebeth, in the seventh year of his reign.

title: Esther 2:17
text: And the king loved Esther above all the women, and she rose in grace and favor in his sight more than all the virgins. And he set the royal crown on her head, and made her queen instead of Vashti.

title: Esther 2:18
text: And the king made a great feast to all his princes and his servants, Esther's feast. And he ordered a release for the provinces, and gave gifts, according to the state of the king.

title: Esther 2:19
text: And when the virgins were gathered the second time, then Mordecai sat in the king's gate.

title: Esther 2:20
text: Esther had not yet revealed her kindred nor her people, as Mordecai had commanded her. For Esther obeyed the command of Mordecai as she did when she was brought up with him.

title: Esther 2:21
text: In those days, while Mordecai sat in the king's gate, two of the king's eunuchs, Bigthan and Teresh, of those who kept the door, were angry and tried to lay a hand on king Ahasuerus.

title: Esther 2:22
text: And the thing was known to Mordecai, who told Esther the queen. And Esther told the king in Mordecai's name.

title: Esther 2:23
text: And when the matter was searched into, it was found out, and the two of them were hanged on a tree. And it was written in the Book of the Matters of the Days before the king.

title: Esther 3:1
text: After these things king Ahasuerus promoted Haman the son of Hammedatha the Agagite, and advanced him, and set his seat above all the princes who [were] with him.

title: Esther 3:2
text: And all the king's servants in the king's gate bowed and worshiped Haman, for the king had so commanded concerning him. But Mordecai did not bow nor worship.

title: Esther 3:3
text: And the king's servants in the king's gate said to Mordecai, Why do you transgress the king's command?

title: Esther 3:4
text: And it happened when they spoke daily to him, and when he did not listen to them, they told Haman, to see if Mordecai's matters would stand. For he had told them that he [was] a Jew.

title: Esther 3:5
text: And when Haman saw that Mordecai did not bow nor worship him, then Haman was full of wrath.

title: Esther 3:6
text: And he scorned to lay hands only on Mordecai, for they had revealed to him the people of Mordecai. And Haman sought to destroy all the Jews throughout the whole kingdom of Ahasuerus, the people of Mordecai.

title: Esther 3:7
text: In the first month, that [is], the month Nisan, in the twelfth year of king Ahasuerus, they cast Pur, the lot, before Haman from day to day, and from month to month, to the twelfth [month], the month Adar.

title: Esther 3:8
text: And Haman said to king Ahasuerus, There is a certain people scattered abroad and dispersed among the people, in all the provinces of your kingdom. And their laws [are] different from all people, neither do they keep the king's laws. And it is not for the king's gain to allow them to live.

title: Esther 3:9
text: If it pleases the king, let it be written that they may be destroyed. And I will pay ten thousand talents of silver to the hands of those who have charge of the business, to bring [it] into the king's treasuries.

title: Esther 3:10
text: And the king took his ring from his hand, and gave it to Haman the son of Hammedatha the Agagite, the Jews' enemy.

title: Esther 3:11
text: And the king said to Haman, The silver [is] given to you, the people also, to do with them as seems good to you.

title: Esther 3:12
text: Then the king's scribes were called on the thirteenth day of the first month, and there was written according to all that Haman had commanded to the king's lieutenants, and to the governors [who were] over every province, and to the rulers of every people of every province, according to the writing of it, and to every people according to their language. It was written in the name of king Ahasuerus and sealed with the king's ring.

title: Esther 3:13
text: And the letters were sent by postal riders into all the king's provinces, to destroy, to kill, and to cause to perish, all Jews, both young and old, little children and women, in one day, on the thirteenth of the twelfth month, which is the month Adar, and [to take] what they owned for a prize.

title: Esther 3:14
text: The copy of the writing, for a command to be given in every province, was published to all people, to be ready for that day.

title: Esther 3:15
text: The posts went out, being hurried by the king's command, and the decree was given in Shushan the palace. And the king and Haman sat down to drink, but the city Shushan was perplexed.

title: Esther 4:1
text: And Mordecai understood all that was done, and Mordecai tore his clothes and put on sackcloth with ashes and went out into the middle of the city, and cried with a loud and bitter cry.

title: Esther 4:2
text: And he even came before the king's gate for none [might] enter into the king's gate clothed with sackcloth.

title: Esther 4:3
text: And in every province, wherever the king's command and his decree came, there [was] great mourning among the Jews, and fasting, and weeping and wailing. And many lay in sackcloth and ashes.

title: Esther 4:4
text: And Esther's servant women and her eunuchs came and told her. And the queen was exceedingly grieved, and she sent clothing to clothe Mordecai, and to take away his sackcloth from him. But he did not receive [it].

title: Esther 4:5
text: And Esther called for Hatach, [one] of the king's eunuchs whom he had appointed to attend on her, and gave him a command to Mordecai to know what it [was] and why it [was].

title: Esther 4:6
text: And Hatach went forth to Mordecai, to the street of the city in front of the king's gate.

title: Esther 4:7
text: And Mordecai told him of all that had happened to him, and of the sum of the silver which Haman had promised to pay to the king's treasuries for the Jews in order to destroy them.

title: Esther 4:8
text: Also he gave him the copy of the writing of the decree which [was] given at Shushan in order to destroy them, to show [it] to Esther and to declare it to her, and to command her that she should go in to the king to make supplication to him, and to seek help for her people.

title: Esther 4:9
text: And Hatach came and told Esther the words of Mordecai.

title: Esther 4:10
text: Again Esther spoke to Hatach, and gave him command to Mordecai.

title: Esther 4:11
text: And the king's servants and the people of the king's provinces know that whoever, whether man or woman, shall come to the king into the inner court, who is not called, [there is] one law of his, execution, except such to whom the king shall hold out the golden scepter so that he may live. But I have not been called to come in to the king these thirty days.

title: Esther 4:12
text: And they told Mordecai Esther's words.

title: Esther 4:13
text: And Mordecai commanded them to answer Esther, Do not think within yourself that you shall escape in the king's house more than all the Jews.

title: Esther 4:14
text: For if you are completely silent at this time, relief and deliverance shall arise to the Jews from another place, but you and your father's house shall be destroyed. And who knows whether you have come to the kingdom for a time like this?

title: Esther 4:15
text: And Esther said to return to Mordecai [this answer],

title: Esther 4:16
text: Go, gather all the Jews who are present in Shushan, and fast for me, and do not eat nor drink three days, night or day. My maidservants and I will also fast in the same way. And so I will go in to the king, which [is] not according to the law. And if I perish, I perish.

title: Esther 4:17
text: And Mordecai passed over and did according to all that Esther had commanded him.

title: Esther 5:1
text: And it happened on the third day, Esther put on royal [clothing], and stood in the inner court of the king's house, across from the king's house. And the king sat on his royal throne in the royal house, across from the gate of the house.

title: Esther 5:2
text: And it happened when the king saw Esther the queen standing in the court, she received favor [in] his sight. And the king held out to Esther the golden scepter in his hand. And Esther drew near and touched the top of the scepter.

title: Esther 5:3
text: And the king said to her, What do you [desire], queen Esther? And what [is] your wish? It shall be given to you even to half of the kingdom.

title: Esther 5:4
text: And Esther answered, If [it is] good to the king, let the king and Haman come today to the banquet which I have prepared for him.

title: Esther 5:5
text: And the king said, Cause Haman to hurry so that he may do as Esther has said. And the king and Haman came to the banquet which Esther had prepared.

title: Esther 5:6
text: And the king said to Esther at the banquet of wine, What [is] your petition that it shall be granted to you? And what [is] your request? It shall be performed even to half of the kingdom.

title: Esther 5:7
text: And Esther answered and said, [As to] my petition and my request,

title: Esther 5:8
text: if I have found favor in the sight of the king, and if it pleases the king to grant my petition and to perform my request, let the king and Haman come to the banquet which I shall prepare for them, and I will do tomorrow as the king has said.

title: Esther 5:9
text: And Haman went forth that day joyful and with a glad heart. But when Haman saw Mordecai in the king's gate, that he did not stand up nor move for him, he was full of fury against Mordecai.

title: Esther 5:10
text: But Haman held himself in. And when he came home, he sent and called [for] his friends and Zeresh his wife.

title: Esther 5:11
text: And Haman told them of the glory of his riches, and his many sons, and all to which the king had promoted him, and how he had advanced him above the princes and servants of the king.

title: Esther 5:12
text: And Haman said, Yes, Esther the queen let [no man] but me come in with the king to the banquet that she had prepared. And also tomorrow I am invited to [her banquet], with the king.

title: Esther 5:13
text: Yet all this avails me nothing as long as I see Mordecai the Jew sitting at the king's gate.

title: Esther 5:14
text: And Zeresh his wife and all his friends said to him, Make a wooden [gallows], fifty cubits high and tomorrow speak to the king that Mordecai may be hanged on it. Then go in merrily with the king to the banquet. And the thing pleased Haman, and he caused the wooden [gallows] to be made.

title: Esther 6:1
text: On that night the king could not sleep, and he commanded to bring the Book of the Records of the Matter of the Days. And they were read before the king.

title: Esther 6:2
text: And it was found written that Mordecai had told of Bigthana and Teresh, two of the king's eunuchs, the keepers of the door who tried to lay a hand on king Ahasuerus.

title: Esther 6:3
text: And the king said, What honor and dignity has been done to Mordecai for this? And the king's servants who served him said, Nothing has been done for him.

title: Esther 6:4
text: And the king said, Who [is] in the court? And Haman had come into the outer court of the king's house to speak to the king to hang Mordecai on the wooden [gallows] which he had prepared for him.

title: Esther 6:5
text: And the king's servants said to him, Behold, Haman stands in the court. And the king said, Let him come in.

title: Esther 6:6
text: So Haman came in. And the king said to him, What shall be done to the man whom the king delights to honor? And Haman thought in his heart, To whom would the king delight to do honor more than to myself?

title: Esther 6:7
text: And Haman answered the king, For the man whom the king delights to honor,

title: Esther 6:8
text: let the royal clothing be brought, which the king wears, and the horse that the king rides on, and the royal crown which is set on his head.

title: Esther 6:9
text: And let this clothing and horse be delivered to the hand of one of the king's most noble princes so that they may dress the man whom the king delights to honor, and bring him on horseback through the streets of the city, and proclaim before him, This is what shall be done to the man whom the king delights to honor.

title: Esther 6:10
text: And the king said to Haman, Make haste! Take the clothing and the horse, as you have said, and do even so to Mordecai the Jew, who sits at the king's gate. Do not fail to do any of all the things you have spoken.

title: Esther 6:11
text: And Haman took the clothing and the horse and dressed Mordecai, and brought him on horseback through the street of the city, and proclaimed before him, This is what shall be done to the man whom the king delights to honor!

title: Esther 6:12
text: And Mordecai came again to the king's gate. But Haman hurried to his house mourning, and having [his] head covered.

title: Esther 6:13
text: And Haman told Zeresh his wife and all his friends every [thing] that had happened to him. Then his wise men and Zeresh his wife said to him, If Mordecai is of the seed of the Jews, before whom you have begun to fall, you shall not prevail against him but shall surely fall before him.

title: Esther 6:14
text: And while they [were] still talking with him, the king's eunuchs came. And they hurried to bring Haman to the banquet which Esther had prepared.

title: Esther 7:1
text: And the king and Haman came to the banquet of Esther the queen.

title: Esther 7:2
text: And the king said again to Esther on the second day of the banquet of wine, What [is] your petition, queen Esther, that it may be granted you? And what [is] your request? And it shall be performed, even to the half of the kingdom.

title: Esther 7:3
text: And Esther the queen answered and said, If I have found favor in your sight, O king, and if it pleases the king, let my life be given me at my petition, and my people at my request.

title: Esther 7:4
text: For we are sold, my people and I, to be destroyed, to be killed, and to perish. But if we had been sold for men-slaves and women-slaves, I would have held my tongue, although the enemy could not make up for the king's damage.

title: Esther 7:5
text: And king Ahasuerus answered and said to Esther the queen, Who [is] he, and where [is] the one who dares presume in his heart to do so?

title: Esther 7:6
text: And Esther said, The man who is our adversary and enemy [is] this wicked Haman. And Haman was afraid before the king and the queen.

title: Esther 7:7
text: And the king, arising from the banquet of wine in his wrath, [went] into the palace garden. And Haman stood up to beg for his life from Esther the queen, for he saw that evil was determined against him by the king.

title: Esther 7:8
text: And the king returned out of the palace garden into the place of the banquet of wine. And Haman had fallen on the bed on which Esther [was]. And the king said, Will he also force the queen before me in the house? As the word went out of the king's mouth, they covered Haman's face.

title: Esther 7:9
text: And Harbonah, one of the eunuchs, said before the king, Also look! the wooden [gallows] fifty cubits high which Haman made for Mordecai, who had spoken good for the king, stands in the house of Haman. Then the king said, Hang him on it!

title: Esther 7:10
text: And they hanged Haman on the wooden [gallows] that he had prepared for Mordecai. And the king's wrath lay down.

title: Esther 8:1
text: On that day king Ahasuerus gave the house of Haman, the Jews' enemy, to Esther the queen. And Mordecai came before the king, for Esther had told what he [was] to her.

title: Esther 8:2
text: And the king took off his ring, which he had taken from Haman, and gave it to Mordecai. And Esther set Mordecai over the house of Haman.

title: Esther 8:3
text: And Esther spoke yet again before the king, and fell down at his feet, and begged him with tears to put away the evil of Haman the Agagite, and his plot which he had plotted against the Jews.

title: Esther 8:4
text: Then the king held out the golden scepter toward Esther. And Esther arose and stood before the king,

title: Esther 8:5
text: and said, If it please the king, and if I have found favor in his sight, and if the thing [is] right before the king, and if I am pleasing in his eyes, let it be written to bring back the documents (a sly plan by Haman the son of Hammedatha the Agagite) which he wrote to destroy the Jews in all the king's provinces.

title: Esther 8:6
text: For how can I bear to see the evil that shall come on my people? Or how can I endure to see the slaughter of my kindred?

title: Esther 8:7
text: And king Ahasuerus said to Esther the queen and to Mordecai the Jew, Behold, I have given Esther the house of Haman, and have hanged him on the wooden [gallows], because he laid his hand on the Jews.

title: Esther 8:8
text: And you write for the Jews as it pleases you, in the king's name, and seal [it] with the king's ring. For the writing which is written in the king's name and sealed with the king's ring, no man may turn back.

title: Esther 8:9
text: Then the king's scribes were called at that time in the third month, the month Sivan, on the twenty-third of it. And it was written according to all that Mordecai commanded to the Jews, and to the lieutenants and the governors and rulers of the provinces from India to Ethiopia, a hundred and twenty-seven provinces, to every province according to the writing of it, and to every people in their writing, and to the Jews according to their writing and according to their language.

title: Esther 8:10
text: And he wrote in the name of king Ahasuerus and sealed [it] with the king's ring. And he sent letters by riders on horseback, riders on royal steeds, stallions, even sons of mares.

title: Esther 8:11
text: In [them] the king granted the Jews in every city to gather themselves, and to stand for their life, to destroy, to kill and to cause to perish, all the power of the people and province who desired to attack them, little ones and women, and [to take] what they owned for a prize,

title: Esther 8:12
text: on one day in all the provinces of king Ahasuerus, on the thirteenth of the twelfth month, which [is] the month Adar.

title: Esther 8:13
text: The copy of the writing for a command to be given in every province [was] announced to all people, even that the Jews should be ready against that day to avenge themselves on their enemies.

title: Esther 8:14
text: The runners, riders on stallions, royal steeds, went out, being hurried and pressed on by the king's command. And the order was given at Shushan the palace.

title: Esther 8:15
text: And Mordecai went out from the presence of the king in royal clothing of blue and white, and with a great crown [of] gold, and with a garment of fine linen and purple. And the city of Shushan rejoiced and was glad.

title: Esther 8:16
text: The Jews had light and gladness and joy and honor.

title: Esther 8:17
text: And in every province, and in every city where the king's command and his order came, the Jews had joy and gladness, a feast and a good day. And many of the people of the land became Jews, for the fear of the Jews fell on them.

title: Esther 9:1
text: And in the twelfth month, the month Adar, on the thirteenth day of the same, when the king's command and his order came to be done, in the day that the enemies of the Jews hoped to have power over them; though it was turned around, so that the Jews had rule over the ones who hated them.

title: Esther 9:2
text: The Jews gathered themselves in their cities throughout all the provinces of king Ahasuerus, in order to lay hand on any who sought their harm. And no man could withstand them, for the fear of them fell on all people.

title: Esther 9:3
text: And all the rulers of the provinces, and the lieutenants and the governors and officers of the king helped the Jews, because the fear of Mordecai fell on them.

title: Esther 9:4
text: For Mordecai [was] great in the house of the king, and his fame went throughout all the provinces. For this man Mordecai was going on and growing greater.

title: Esther 9:5
text: And the Jews struck all their enemies with the stroke of the sword, and slaughter, and destruction, and did what they would to those who hated them.

title: Esther 9:6
text: And in Shushan the palace the Jews killed and destroyed five hundred men.

title: Esther 9:7
text: And Parshandatha, and Dalphon, and Aspatha,

title: Esther 9:8
text: and Poratha, and Adalia, and Aridatha,

title: Esther 9:9
text: and Parmashta, and Arisai, and Aridai, and Vajezatha,

title: Esther 9:10
text: they killed the ten sons of Haman the son of Hammedatha, the enemy of the Jews. But they did not lay their hands on the spoil.

title: Esther 9:11
text: On that day the number of those who were killed in Shushan the palace was brought before the king.

title: Esther 9:12
text: And the king said to Esther the queen, The Jews have killed and destroyed five hundred men in Shushan the palace, and the ten sons of Haman. What have they done in the rest of the king's provinces? And what [is] your petition, that it may be granted you? Or what further request do you have? And it shall be done.

title: Esther 9:13
text: Then Esther said, If it pleases the king, let it be granted to the Jews in Shushan to do tomorrow also according to this day's decree, and let Haman's ten sons be hanged on the wooden [gallows].

title: Esther 9:14
text: And the king commanded it to be done. And the order was given at Shushan, and they hanged Haman's ten sons.

title: Esther 9:15
text: For the Jews in Shushan gathered themselves on the fourteenth day also of the month Adar, and killed three hundred men at Shushan. But they did not lay their hands on the spoil.

title: Esther 9:16
text: But the rest of the Jews in the king's provinces gathered themselves and stood for their lives, and had rest from their enemies, and killed seventy-five thousand of their foes. But they did not lay their hands on the spoil.

title: Esther 9:17
text: And on the thirteenth day of the month Adar, and on the fourteenth day of the same, they rested and made it a day of feasting and gladness.

title: Esther 9:18
text: But the Jews at Shushan gathered on the thirteenth of it and on the fourteenth of it. And on the fifteenth of the same, they rested and made it a day of feasting and gladness.

title: Esther 9:19
text: Therefore the Jews of the villages, who lived in the unwalled towns, made the fourteenth day of the month Adar [a day of] gladness and feasting, and a good day, and [a day of] sending portions to one another.

title: Esther 9:20
text: And Mordecai wrote these things, and sent letters to all the Jews in all the provinces of the king Ahasuerus, near and far,

title: Esther 9:21
text: to establish among them that they should keep the fourteenth day of the month Adar, and the fifteenth day of the same, yearly,

title: Esther 9:22
text: as the days in which the Jews rested from their enemies, and the month which was turned to them from sorrow to joy, and from mourning into a good day that they should make them days of feasting and joy, and of sending portions to one another, and gifts to the poor.

title: Esther 9:23
text: And the Jews undertook to do as they had begun, and as Mordecai had written to them

title: Esther 9:24
text: because Haman the son of Hammedatha the Agagite, the enemy of all the Jews, had plotted against the Jews to destroy them, and had cast Pur, the lot, to finish them and to destroy them.

title: Esther 9:25
text: But when [Esther] came before the king, he commanded by letters that his wicked plot which he had plotted against the Jews should return on his own head, and that he and his sons should be hanged on the wooden [gallows].

title: Esther 9:26
text: Therefore, they called these days Purim after the name of Pur. Therefore, for all the words of this letter, and which they had seen concerning this matter, and which had come to them,

title: Esther 9:27
text: the Jews ordained, and took on them and on their seed, and on all such as joined themselves to them, so as it should not fail, that they would keep these two days according to their writing, and according to their time every year

title: Esther 9:28
text: and [that] these days [should be] remembered and kept throughout every generation, every family, every province, and every city and these days of Purim should not fail from among the Jews, nor the memorial of them perish from their seed.

title: Esther 9:29
text: And Esther the queen, the daughter of Abihail, and Mordecai the Jew, wrote with all authority to confirm this second letter of Purim.

title: Esther 9:30
text: And he sent the letters to all the Jews, to the hundred and twenty-seven provinces of the kingdom of Ahasuerus, [with] words of peace and truth,

title: Esther 9:31
text: in order to confirm these days of Purim in their [set] times, according as Mordecai the Jew and Esther the queen had ordered them, and as they had decreed for themselves and for their seed the matters of the fastings and of their cry.

title: Esther 9:32
text: And the order of Esther confirmed these matters of Purim. And it was written in the book.

title: Esther 10:1
text: And king Ahasuerus laid a tax on the land and [on] the isles of the sea.

title: Esther 10:2
text: And all the acts of his power and of might, and the declaration of the greatness of Mordecai, with which the king made him great, [are] they not written in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Media and Persia?

title: Esther 10:3
text: For Mordecai the Jew [was] next to king Ahasuerus and great among the Jews, and pleasing to the multitude of his brothers, seeking the wealth of his people and speaking peace to all his seed.

title: Job 1:1
text: There was a man in the land of Uz, whose name [was] Job. And that man was perfect and upright, and one who feared God and turned aside from evil.

title: Job 1:2
text: And there were born to him seven sons and three daughters.

title: Job 1:3
text: And his possessions were seven thousand sheep and three thousand camels, and five hundred yoke of oxen, and five hundred she asses, and a very great household, so that this man was the greatest of all the men of the east.

title: Job 1:4
text: And his sons went and feasted in the house of each one on his day. And they sent and called for their three sisters to eat and to drink with them.

title: Job 1:5
text: And when they had gone around the day of feasting, Job sent and sanctified them, and rose up early in the morning and offered burnt offerings [according to] the number of them all. For Job said, It may be that my sons have sinned and cursed God in their hearts. So Job did always.

title: Job 1:6
text: And a day came when the sons of God came to present themselves before the LORD. And Satan also came among them.

title: Job 1:7
text: And the LORD said to Satan, From where do you come? Then Satan answered the LORD and said, From going to and fro in the earth, and from walking up and down in it.

title: Job 1:8
text: And the LORD said to Satan, Have you set your heart against My servant Job, because [there is] none like him in the earth, a perfect and upright man, one who fears God and turns away from evil?

title: Job 1:9
text: And Satan answered the LORD and said, Does Job fear God for nothing?

title: Job 1:10
text: Have You not made a hedge around him, and around his house, and around all that he has on every side? You have blessed the work of his hands, and his livestock have increased in the land.

title: Job 1:11
text: But put forth Your hand now, and touch all that he has, and he will curse You to Your face.

title: Job 1:12
text: And the LORD said to Satan, Behold, all that he has [is] in your power. Only do not lay your hand upon him. And Satan went forth from the presence of the LORD.

title: Job 1:13
text: And a day came when his sons and his daughters [were] eating and drinking wine in their oldest brother's house.

title: Job 1:14
text: And there came a messenger to Job and said, The oxen were plowing, and the asses feeding beside them.

title: Job 1:15
text: And the Sabeans fell [on] and took them away. Yea, they have killed the servants with the edge of the sword. And I only have escaped alone to tell you.

title: Job 1:16
text: While he [was] still speaking, there also came [another] and said, The fire of God has fallen from the heavens and has burned up the sheep and the servants, and destroyed them. And I only have escaped alone to tell you.

title: Job 1:17
text: While he [was] still speaking, there also came [another] and said, The Chaldeans made out three bands and swooped down upon the camels, and have carried them away, yea, and have killed the servants with the edge of the sword. And I only have escaped alone to tell you.

title: Job 1:18
text: While he [was] still speaking, there also came another and said, Your sons and your daughters were eating and drinking wine in their oldest brother's house.

title: Job 1:19
text: And, behold, a great wind came from the wilderness and struck the four corners of the house, and it fell upon the young men, and they are dead. And I only have escaped alone to tell you.

title: Job 1:20
text: And Job arose, and tore his robe, and shaved his head, and fell down upon the ground and worshiped.

title: Job 1:21
text: And he said, I came naked out of my mother's womb, and naked shall I return there. The LORD gave, and the LORD has taken away. Blessed [be] the name of the LORD.

title: Job 1:22
text: In all this Job did not sin, nor charge God foolishly.

title: Job 2:1
text: And it happened that a day came when the sons of God came to present themselves before the LORD. And Satan also came among them to present himself before the LORD.

title: Job 2:2
text: And the LORD said to Satan, From where do you come? And Satan answered the LORD and said, From going to and fro in the earth, and from walking up and down in it.

title: Job 2:3
text: And the LORD said unto Satan, Have you set your heart on My servant Job, that [there is] none like him in the earth, a perfect and an upright man, one who fears God and turns away from evil? And still he is keeping hold of his integrity, although you moved Me against him to destroy him without cause.

title: Job 2:4
text: And Satan answered the LORD and said, Skin for skin, yea, all that a man has he will give for his life.

title: Job 2:5
text: But indeed put forth Your hand now, and touch his bone and his flesh, and he will curse You to Your face.

title: Job 2:6
text: And the LORD said to Satan, Behold, he [is] in your hand, but save his life.

title: Job 2:7
text: And Satan went forth from the presence of the LORD and struck Job with sore boils from the sole of his foot to the top of his head.

title: Job 2:8
text: And he took a broken piece of pottery to scrape himself with. And he sat down among the ashes.

title: Job 2:9
text: And his wife said to him, Do you still hold to your integrity? Curse God and die!

title: Job 2:10
text: But he said to her, You speak as one of the foolish ones speak. What? Shall we receive good at the hand of God, and shall we not receive evil? In all this Job did not sin with his lips.

title: Job 2:11
text: And Job's three friends heard [of] all this evil that had come upon him, and they each one came from his own place: Eliphaz the Temanite, and Bildad the Shuhite, and Zophar the Naamathite. For they had met together to come to mourn with him and to comfort him.

title: Job 2:12
text: And when they lifted up their eyes afar off, and did not know him, they lifted up their voice and wept. And each one tore his robe, and [they] sprinkled dust upon their heads toward Heaven.

title: Job 2:13
text: And they sat down with him upon the ground seven days and seven nights. And no one spoke a word to him, for they saw that [his] grief was very great.

title: Job 3:1
text: After this Job opened his mouth and cursed his day.

title: Job 3:2
text: And Job spoke and said,

title: Job 3:3
text: Let the day perish in [which] I was born, and the night [which] said, A man-child is conceived.

title: Job 3:4
text: Let that day be darkness. Let not God look upon it from above, neither let the light shine upon it.

title: Job 3:5
text: Let darkness and the shadow of death claim it. Let a cloud dwell upon it; Let the blackness of the day terrify it.

title: Job 3:6
text: As [for] that night, let darkness seize upon it. Let it not rejoice among the days of the year, Let it not come into the number of the months.

title: Job 3:7
text: Lo, let that night be barren; let no joyful voice come in it.

title: Job 3:8
text: Let those curse it who curse the day, who are ready to stir up Leviathan.

title: Job 3:9
text: Let the stars of its twilight be dark; let it look for light, but have none. Let it not see the eyelids of the dawn.

title: Job 3:10
text: For it did not shut up the doors of my [mother's] womb, nor hide sorrow from my eyes.

title: Job 3:11
text: Why did I not die from the womb, come from the womb and expire?

title: Job 3:12
text: Why did the knees go before me; or why the breasts, that I should suck?

title: Job 3:13
text: For now I should have lain still and been quiet; I should have slept. Then I would have been at rest

title: Job 3:14
text: with kings and wise men of the earth, who built ruins for themselves,

title: Job 3:15
text: or with princes who had gold, who filled their houses with silver;

title: Job 3:16
text: or as a hidden untimely birth I would not have been, like infants who did not see light.

title: Job 3:17
text: There the wicked cease [from] troubling, and there the weary are at rest;

title: Job 3:18
text: the prisoners are at rest together; they hear not the voice of the slave driver.

title: Job 3:19
text: The small and the great are there, and the slave [is] free from his master.

title: Job 3:20
text: Why is light given to one who is in misery, and life to the bitter [in] soul,

title: Job 3:21
text: who is waiting for death, but [it] comes not; and dig for it more than [for] treasures?

title: Job 3:22
text: They are rejoicing to exultation. They are glad when they can find the grave.

title: Job 3:23
text: To a man whose way is hidden, God has made a hedge about him.

title: Job 3:24
text: For my sighing comes before I eat, and my groanings are poured out like the waters.

title: Job 3:25
text: For the thing which I greatly feared has come upon me, and that which I was afraid of has come to me.

title: Job 3:26
text: I was not in safety, nor did I have rest, nor was I quiet; yet trouble comes.

title: Job 4:1
text: And Eliphaz the Temanite answered:

title: Job 4:2
text: Shall one try a word with you, you [who] are weary? But who can hold back with words?

title: Job 4:3
text: Behold, you have instructed many, and you have made the weak hands strong.

title: Job 4:4
text: Your words have upheld him who was falling, and you have made strong the feeble knees.

title: Job 4:5
text: But now it has come upon you, and you faint. It touches you, and you are troubled.

title: Job 4:6
text: [Is] not your reverence your hope? Is not your hope the uprightness of your ways?

title: Job 4:7
text: Remember, please, who [ever] perished, being innocent? Or where were the righteous cut off?

title: Job 4:8
text: As I have seen, the ones who plow iniquity and sow wickedness reap the same.

title: Job 4:9
text: By the blast of God they perish, and by the breath of His nostrils they are destroyed.

title: Job 4:10
text: The roar of the lion, and the voice of the fierce lion, and the teeth of the young lions, are broken.

title: Job 4:11
text: The strong lion perishes for lack of prey, and the strong lion's cubs are scattered abroad.

title: Job 4:12
text: And a word was secretly brought to me, and my ear received a little of it.

title: Job 4:13
text: In thoughts from the visions of the night, when deep sleep falls upon men,

title: Job 4:14
text: fear came upon me, and trembling, which made all my bones shake.

title: Job 4:15
text: And a spirit passed before my face; the hair of my flesh stood up.

title: Job 4:16
text: It stood still, but I could not tell the form of it. An image [was] before my eyes; silence; then I heard a voice,

title: Job 4:17
text: Shall mortal [man] be more just than God? Shall a man be more pure than his Maker?

title: Job 4:18
text: Behold, He puts no trust in His servants, and His angels He charges with folly!

title: Job 4:19
text: How much less [in] those who live in houses of clay, whose foundation [is] in the dust, [who] are crushed before the moth?

title: Job 4:20
text: They are destroyed from morning till evening; they perish forever without anyone caring.

title: Job 4:21
text: Is not their tent cord plucked up within them? They die, but not with wisdom.

title: Job 5:1
text: Call now, is there anyone who will answer you? And to which of the saints will you turn?

title: Job 5:2
text: For vexation kills the fool, and envy slays the simple one.

title: Job 5:3
text: I have seen the fool taking root, but suddenly I cursed his dwelling place.

title: Job 5:4
text: His children are far from safety, and they are crushed in the gate, nor [is there] any to deliver [them].

title: Job 5:5
text: Their harvest the hungry eats, and takes it even out of the thorns; and the snare swallows up their wealth.

title: Job 5:6
text: For affliction does not come forth from the dust, nor does trouble spring up out of the ground;

title: Job 5:7
text: but man is born to trouble, as the sparks fly upward.

title: Job 5:8
text: Truly, I would seek to God, and to God I would put my plea,

title: Job 5:9
text: [Who is] doing great things, even beyond searching; marvelous things without number,

title: Job 5:10
text: who gives rain on the earth and sends waters on the field,

title: Job 5:11
text: to set on high those who are low, so that those who mourn may be lifted up [to] safety;

title: Job 5:12
text: frustrating the plans of the crafty, nor did their hands do wisely.

title: Job 5:13
text: [He] takes the wise in their own craftiness; and the counsel of the wily is carried headlong.

title: Job 5:14
text: They meet with darkness in the day time, and grope in the noonday as in the night.

title: Job 5:15
text: But He saves the poor from the sword, from their mouth, and from the hand of the mighty.

title: Job 5:16
text: And there is hope for the weak, and injustice shuts her mouth.

title: Job 5:17
text: Behold, blessed [is] the man whom God corrects. Therefore do not despise the chastening of the Almighty.

title: Job 5:18
text: For He makes sore, and binds up; He wounds, and His hands make whole.

title: Job 5:19
text: He will deliver you in six troubles; yea, in seven no evil shall touch you.

title: Job 5:20
text: In famine He shall redeem you from death; and in war from the power of the sword.

title: Job 5:21
text: You shall be hidden from the whip of the tongue; neither shall you be afraid of robbery when it comes.

title: Job 5:22
text: At destruction and famine you shall laugh; neither shall you be afraid of the beasts of the earth.

title: Job 5:23
text: For you [shall be] in covenant with the stones of the field; and the beasts of the field shall be at peace with you.

title: Job 5:24
text: And you shall know that your tent [is in] peace; and you shall visit your fold, and shall miss nothing.

title: Job 5:25
text: And [you] shall know that your seed [will be] numerous, and your offspring as the grass of the earth.

title: Job 5:26
text: You shall come to [your] grave in a full age, like a shock of grain comes in its season.

title: Job 5:27
text: Behold this: we have searched it; it is so. Hear it and know for yourself.

title: Job 6:1
text: And Job answered and said,

title: Job 6:2
text: Oh that my grief were but weighed, and my ruin laid in the balances together!

title: Job 6:3
text: For now it would be heavier than the sand of the sea; therefore my words have been rash.

title: Job 6:4
text: For the arrows of the Almighty [are] within me, their fury [is] drinking my spirit; the terrors of God are set against me.

title: Job 6:5
text: Does the wild ass bray [when he has] grass? Or does the ox low over his fodder?

title: Job 6:6
text: Can that which has no taste be eaten without salt? Or is there taste in the white of an egg?

title: Job 6:7
text: My soul refuses to touch them; they [are] sickening food to me.

title: Job 6:8
text: Oh that I might have my desire, and that God would grant the thing that I long for!

title: Job 6:9
text: Even that it would please God to destroy me; that He would loose His hand and cut me off!

title: Job 6:10
text: And it is yet my comfort; yea, I would rejoice in pain, though He did not spare me; for I have not hidden the words of the Holy One.

title: Job 6:11
text: What [is] my strength, that I should hope? And what [is] my end, that I should be patient?

title: Job 6:12
text: [Is] my strength the strength of stones? Or [is] my flesh bronze?

title: Job 6:13
text: [Is] not my help in me? And is wisdom fully driven away from me?

title: Job 6:14
text: To him who is afflicted, pity is [due] from his friend, but he forsakes the fear of the Almighty.

title: Job 6:15
text: My brothers have dealt deceitfully as a torrent; they pass away as the streams of torrents,

title: Job 6:16
text: [torrents] black from ice, in which the snow hides itself.

title: Job 6:17
text: When they become warm, they go away; when it is hot, they vanish out of their place.

title: Job 6:18
text: The paths of their way are turned aside; they go to nothing and are lost.

title: Job 6:19
text: The troops of Tema looked; the companies of Sheba hoped for them.

title: Job 6:20
text: They were ashamed because they had hoped; they came there and were ashamed.

title: Job 6:21
text: Surely now you are like them; you see [my] casting down, and are afraid.

title: Job 6:22
text: Did I say, Give to me? or, Offer a bribe for me from your wealth;

title: Job 6:23
text: or, Deliver me from the enemy's hand; or, Redeem me from the hand of the mighty?

title: Job 6:24
text: Teach me, and I will be silent; and cause me to understand where I have gone astray.

title: Job 6:25
text: Right words are powerful, but what does your arguing argue?

title: Job 6:26
text: Do you intend to criticize words, and the speeches of one who is hopeless, [that are] as wind?

title: Job 6:27
text: Yea, you cause [anger] to fall on the fatherless, and you dig [a pit] for your friend.

title: Job 6:28
text: And now, please look on me; for if I lie, [it is] before your face.

title: Job 6:29
text: Turn back, please let there be no sin; yea, return again, my righteousness [is] in this matter.

title: Job 6:30
text: Is there wrong in my tongue? Cannot my taste discern desirable things?

title: Job 7:1
text: [Is there] not a warfare to man on earth? [Are] not his days also like the days of a hireling?

title: Job 7:2
text: As a servant earnestly desires the shadow, and as a hireling looks for his wages,

title: Job 7:3
text: so I am made to possess months of vanity, and weary nights are appointed to me.

title: Job 7:4
text: When I lie down, I say, When shall I rise? But the night is long, and I am full of tossing to and fro until the dawning of the day.

title: Job 7:5
text: My flesh is clothed with worms and clods of dust; my skin is broken and has run [afresh].

title: Job 7:6
text: My days are swifter than a weaver's shuttle, and are ended without hope.

title: Job 7:7
text: Remember that my life [is] a breath; my eye shall no more see good.

title: Job 7:8
text: The eye of him who has seen me shall see me no [more]; Your eyes [are] on me, and I [am] gone.

title: Job 7:9
text: [As] the cloud falls and vanishes away, so he who goes down to the grave shall come up no [more].

title: Job 7:10
text: He shall return no more to his house, nor shall his place know him any more.

title: Job 7:11
text: Therefore I will not hold my mouth; I will speak in the trouble of my spirit; I will complain in the bitterness of my soul.

title: Job 7:12
text: Am I like the sea, or a whale, that You set a watch over me?

title: Job 7:13
text: When I say, My bed shall comfort me, my couch shall ease my complaint,

title: Job 7:14
text: then You scare me with dreams, and terrify me with visions;

title: Job 7:15
text: so that my soul chooses strangling, death rather than my life.

title: Job 7:16
text: I despise [them]; I will not live always; let me alone, for my days [are] vanity.

title: Job 7:17
text: What [is] man, that You should magnify him, and that You should set Your heart on him,

title: Job 7:18
text: and visit him every morning, trying him every moment?

title: Job 7:19
text: Until when will You look away from me, nor let me alone until I swallow down my spittle?

title: Job 7:20
text: I have sinned. What shall I do to You, O Watcher of men? Why have You set me as a target for You, so that I am a burden to myself?

title: Job 7:21
text: And why do You not pardon my transgression, and take away my iniquity? For now I shall sleep in the dust, and You shall seek me in the morning, but I [shall] not be.

title: Job 8:1
text: And Bildad the Shuhite answered and said,

title: Job 8:2
text: How long will you speak these things, since the words of your mouth [are like] a strong wind?

title: Job 8:3
text: Does God pervert judgment? Or does the Almighty pervert justice?

title: Job 8:4
text: If your sons have sinned against Him, and if He has cast them away for their transgression,

title: Job 8:5
text: if you would seek earnestly to God and make your prayer to the Almighty;

title: Job 8:6
text: if you [were] pure and upright, surely now He would awake for you, and make the dwelling-place of your righteousness blessed.

title: Job 8:7
text: And if your beginning was small, yet your end would greatly increase.

title: Job 8:8
text: For please ask of the former age, and prepare yourself to the search of their fathers,

title: Job 8:9
text: for we [are but of] yesterday and know nothing, because our days on earth [are] a shadow.

title: Job 8:10
text: Shall they not teach you, [and] tell you, and speak words out of their heart?

title: Job 8:11
text: Can the rush grow up without mire? Can the reed-grass grow without water?

title: Job 8:12
text: While it [is] yet in its greenness, and not cut down, it dries out before any [other] herb.

title: Job 8:13
text: So are the paths of all who forget God; and the hope of the ungodly shall perish.

title: Job 8:14
text: His hope shall be cut off, and his trust [shall be] in a spider's web.

title: Job 8:15
text: He shall lean on his house, but it shall not stand; he shall hold fast to it, but it shall not endure.

title: Job 8:16
text: He [is] moist before the sun, and his branches shoot forth in his garden.

title: Job 8:17
text: His roots are wrapped around the heap, [and] he sees the place of stones.

title: Job 8:18
text: If he is destroyed from his place, then it shall deny him: I have not seen you.

title: Job 8:19
text: Behold, this [is] the joy of his way, and out of the earth shall others grow.

title: Job 8:20
text: Behold, God will not cast away the innocent, nor will He help the evildoers,

title: Job 8:21
text: until He fills your mouth with laughter, and your lips with rejoicing.

title: Job 8:22
text: Those who hate you shall be clothed with shame; and the tent of the wicked [shall be] no more.

title: Job 9:1
text: And Job answered and said,

title: Job 9:2
text: Truly I know [it is so], but how can man be just with God?

title: Job 9:3
text: If he will argue with Him, he cannot answer Him one of a thousand.

title: Job 9:4
text: [He is] wise in heart, and mighty in strength. Who has hardened [himself] against Him and been blessed;

title: Job 9:5
text: [He] who removes the mountains, and they know it not, when He overturns them in His anger;

title: Job 9:6
text: [He] who shakes the earth out of its place, and the pillars of it tremble;

title: Job 9:7
text: the one speaking to the sun, and it does not rise; and seals up the stars;

title: Job 9:8
text: who alone stretches out the heavens, and walks on the waves of the sea;

title: Job 9:9
text: who made the Bear, Orion, and Pleiades, and the chambers of the south;

title: Job 9:10
text: who is doing great things past finding out; yea, marvelous things without number?

title: Job 9:11
text: Behold! He goes by me, and I do not see [Him]; He passes on also, but I do not perceive Him.

title: Job 9:12
text: Behold, He takes away; who can turn Him back? Who will say to Him, What are You doing?

title: Job 9:13
text: God will not withdraw His anger; the helpers of pride stoop under Him.

title: Job 9:14
text: How much less shall I answer Him, [and] choose my arguments with Him?

title: Job 9:15
text: Whom, though I were righteous, [yet] I would not answer; I seek mercy for my judgment.

title: Job 9:16
text: If I had called and He had answered me, yet would I not believe that He had listened to my voice;

title: Job 9:17
text: [He] who breaks me with a tempest, and multiplies my wounds without cause;

title: Job 9:18
text: [who] will not allow me to take my breath, but fills me with bitterness.

title: Job 9:19
text: If [I speak] of strength, lo, [He is] mighty! And if of judgment, who shall set me a time?

title: Job 9:20
text: If I justify myself, my own mouth shall condemn me; [though] I [am] perfect, He shall declare me perverse.

title: Job 9:21
text: [Though] I [were] perfect, yet I would not know my soul. I would despise my life.

title: Job 9:22
text: It [is] One, therefore I said, He is consuming the perfect and the wicked.

title: Job 9:23
text: If the whip kills suddenly, He will mock at the calamity of the innocent.

title: Job 9:24
text: The earth is given into the hand of the wicked; He covers the faces of its judges; if it [is] not [He], then who [is] it?

title: Job 9:25
text: Now my days are swifter than a runner; they flee away, they see no good.

title: Job 9:26
text: They have passed away like the swift ships; like the eagle who swoops on the prey.

title: Job 9:27
text: If I say, I will forget my complaint, I will depart from my heaviness and be of good cheer,

title: Job 9:28
text: I am afraid of all my sorrows; I know that You will not hold me innocent.

title: Job 9:29
text: I have been condemned; why then should I labor in vain?

title: Job 9:30
text: If I wash myself with snow water, and make my hands ever so clean,

title: Job 9:31
text: yet You will plunge me into the ditch and my own clothes shall despise me.

title: Job 9:32
text: For [He is] not a man, as I [am, that] I should answer Him, [that] we should come together in judgment;

title: Job 9:33
text: there is no mediator between us, [who] might lay his hand on us both.

title: Job 9:34
text: Let Him take His rod away from me, and let not His fear make me afraid;

title: Job 9:35
text: [then] would I speak and not fear Him; for [it is] not so with me.

title: Job 10:1
text: My soul is weary of my life; I will leave my complaint on my self; I will speak in the bitterness of my soul.

title: Job 10:2
text: I will say to God, Do not condemn me; make me know why You contend with me.

title: Job 10:3
text: Is [it] good to You that You should press down, that You should despise the work of Your hands, and shine on the counsel of the wicked?

title: Job 10:4
text: [Have] You eyes of flesh? Or do You see as a man sees?

title: Job 10:5
text: [Are] Your days like the days of man? [Are] Your years like man's days,

title: Job 10:6
text: that You seek out my iniquity, and search for my sin?

title: Job 10:7
text: You know that I am not wicked; and [there is] none who can deliver out of Your hand.

title: Job 10:8
text: Your hands have made me and shaped me, together all around; yet You destroy me.

title: Job 10:9
text: Remember, I beseech You, that You have formed me as the clay; and will You bring me into the dust again?

title: Job 10:10
text: Have You not poured me out like milk, and curdled me like cheese?

title: Job 10:11
text: You have clothed me with skin and flesh, and have fenced me with bones and sinews.

title: Job 10:12
text: You have granted me life and favor, and Your providence has preserved my spirit.

title: Job 10:13
text: And these have You hidden in Your heart; I know that this [was] with You.

title: Job 10:14
text: If I sin, then You mark me, and You will not acquit me from my iniquity.

title: Job 10:15
text: If I am wicked, woe to me; and [if] I am righteous, I will not lift up my head [being] filled with shame, and looking on my affliction.

title: Job 10:16
text: For it increases! You hunt me as a fierce lion; and again You show Yourself marvelous on me.

title: Job 10:17
text: You renew Your witnesses against me, and increase Your anger on me; changes and warfare [are] against me.

title: Job 10:18
text: Why then have You brought me from the womb? Oh that I had given up the spirit, and no eye had seen me!

title: Job 10:19
text: I should have been as though I had not been; I would have been carried from the womb to the grave.

title: Job 10:20
text: Are not my days few? Cease [then, and] let me alone, that I may take comfort a little,

title: Job 10:21
text: before I go, and I shall not return, even to the land of darkness and the shadow of death;

title: Job 10:22
text: a land of obscurity, the darkness of the shadow of death, without any order, and the shining [is] as darkness.

title: Job 11:1
text: And Zophar the Naamathite answered and said,

title: Job 11:2
text: Should not the multitude of words be answered? And should a man full of talk be justified?

title: Job 11:3
text: Should your lies make men silent? And will you mock and no one make [you] ashamed?

title: Job 11:4
text: For you have said, My doctrine [is] pure, and I am clean in Your eyes.

title: Job 11:5
text: But who will grant that God would speak, and open His lips against you,

title: Job 11:6
text: and would tell you the secrets of His wisdom, that sound wisdom [is] manifold? Know therefore that God forgets for you [some] of your iniquity.

title: Job 11:7
text: Can you by searching find out God? Can you perfectly find out the Almighty?

title: Job 11:8
text: Heights of the heavens! What can you do? [It is] deeper than hell, what can you know?

title: Job 11:9
text: The measure of it [is] longer than the earth, and broader than the sea.

title: Job 11:10
text: If He passes through and shuts up, or gathers together, then who can turn Him back?

title: Job 11:11
text: For He knows vain men; and when He sees wickedness, will He not search [it]?

title: Job 11:12
text: For foolish man would be wise, and man is born a wild ass's colt.

title: Job 11:13
text: If you prepare your heart and stretch out your hands toward Him;

title: Job 11:14
text: if iniquity [is] in your hand, put it far away, and do not let wickedness dwell in your tents;

title: Job 11:15
text: surely then you shall lift up your face without spot; yea, you shall be steadfast and shall not fear;

title: Job 11:16
text: for you shall forget [your] misery, and you shall remember [it] as waters that pass away.

title: Job 11:17
text: And [your] lifetime shall be clearer than the noonday; though [there be] darkness, you shall be as the morning.

title: Job 11:18
text: And you shall be safe, because there is hope; yea, you shall look around [you], and you shall take your rest in safety.

title: Job 11:19
text: You shall lie down, and none [shall] make you afraid. Yea, many shall seek your favor.

title: Job 11:20
text: But the eyes of the wicked shall fail, and they shall have no escape, and their hope [shall be like] the giving up of the spirit.

title: Job 12:1
text: And Job answered and said,

title: Job 12:2
text: For truly you [are] the people, and wisdom will die with you.

title: Job 12:3
text: But I have understanding as well as you; I do not fall [short] of you; yes, who does not know such things as these?

title: Job 12:4
text: I [am] a laughing-stock to his friends; who calls on God, and He answers him; the just, the upright one [is] a mockery;

title: Job 12:5
text: a flaming brand despised in the thoughts of him who feels secure; [it is] ready for those with slipping feet.

title: Job 12:6
text: The tents of robbers are at peace, and those who provoke God [are] secure, in whatever God brings to their hand.

title: Job 12:7
text: But now ask the animals, and they shall teach you; and the birds of the air, and they shall tell you;

title: Job 12:8
text: or speak to the earth, and it shall teach you; and the fish of the sea shall declare [it] to you;

title: Job 12:9
text: who of all these does not know that the hand of the LORD has done this?

title: Job 12:10
text: In whose hand [is] the soul of every living thing, and the breath of all flesh, [even] of man?

title: Job 12:11
text: Does not the ear try words? And does not the mouth taste its food?

title: Job 12:12
text: With the aged [is] wisdom, and understanding in length of days.

title: Job 12:13
text: With Him [is] wisdom and strength; He has wisdom and understanding.

title: Job 12:14
text: Behold, He breaks down, and it can not be built up again; He shuts up a man, and no one opens.

title: Job 12:15
text: Behold, He withholds the waters, and they dry up; also He sends them out, and they overturn the earth.

title: Job 12:16
text: With Him [is] strength and sound wisdom; the deceived and the deceiver [are] His.

title: Job 12:17
text: He leads wise men away stripped, and makes the judges fools.

title: Job 12:18
text: He cuts away the bonds of kings, and binds their loins with a girdle.

title: Job 12:19
text: He leads priests away stripped, and overthrows the mighty.

title: Job 12:20
text: [He] removes the speech of the men of trust, and takes away the understanding of the aged.

title: Job 12:21
text: He pours scorn on princes, and unties the belt of the mighty.

title: Job 12:22
text: He discovers deep things out of darkness, and brings the shadow of death to light.

title: Job 12:23
text: He gives greatness to the nations, and destroys them. He spreads out the nations, and leads them away.

title: Job 12:24
text: He takes away the heart of the chief of the people of the land, and causes them to wander in a wilderness [where there is] no path.

title: Job 12:25
text: They grope in the dark without light, and He makes them to stagger like [a] drunkard.

title: Job 13:1
text: Lo, my eye has seen all this, my ear has heard and understood it.

title: Job 13:2
text: What you know, I know [also]; I do not fall [short] of you.

title: Job 13:3
text: Surely I would speak to the Almighty, and I desire to argue my case before God.

title: Job 13:4
text: But you [are] imputers of lies; you [are] all worthless healers.

title: Job 13:5
text: Oh that you would stop speaking entirely! And it would be your wisdom.

title: Job 13:6
text: Hear now my reasoning, and listen to the pleadings of my lips.

title: Job 13:7
text: Would you speak unrighteously for God, and talk deceitfully for Him?

title: Job 13:8
text: Will you lift up His person, or contend for God?

title: Job 13:9
text: Is it good that He should search you out? Or as one man mocks another, do you mock Him?

title: Job 13:10
text: He will surely blame you, if you secretly lift up persons.

title: Job 13:11
text: Shall not His highness make you afraid, and His dread fall on you?

title: Job 13:12
text: Your remembered sayings [are] like ashes, your bodies like bodies of clay.

title: Job 13:13
text: Be quiet. Let me alone so that I may speak, and let come on me what may.

title: Job 13:14
text: Why do I take my flesh in my teeth and put my life in my hand?

title: Job 13:15
text: Though he slay me, I will not wait, but I will maintain my own ways before Him.

title: Job 13:16
text: He also [is] my salvation, for an ungodly one shall not come before Him.

title: Job 13:17
text: Listen carefully to my words, and let what I say be in your ears.

title: Job 13:18
text: Behold now, I have set [my] cause in order; I know that I shall be justified.

title: Job 13:19
text: Who [is] he [that] will plead for me, for now, I would be quiet and expire.

title: Job 13:20
text: Only do not do two [things] to me; then I will not hide myself from You.

title: Job 13:21
text: Withdraw Your hand far from me, and let not Your fear make me afraid.

title: Job 13:22
text: Then call, and I will answer; or let me speak, and answer You me.

title: Job 13:23
text: How many [are] my iniquities and sins? Make known my transgressions and my sin.

title: Job 13:24
text: Why do You hide Your face, and hold me for Your enemy?

title: Job 13:25
text: Will You terrify a leaf driven to and fro? Will You pursue the dry stubble?

title: Job 13:26
text: For You write bitter things against me, and make me to possess the sins of my youth.

title: Job 13:27
text: You put my feet also in the stocks, and look closely to all my paths; You set a limit for the soles of my feet.

title: Job 13:28
text: And he wears out like a rotten thing, like a garment that a moth eats.

title: Job 14:1
text: Man born of woman [is] of few days, and full of trouble.

title: Job 14:2
text: He comes forth like a flower, and withers; he also flees as a shadow, and does not stand.

title: Job 14:3
text: And You open Your eyes on such a one, and bring me into judgment with You.

title: Job 14:4
text: Who can bring a clean [thing] out of an unclean? No one!

title: Job 14:5
text: For his days [are] fixed, the number of his months [is] with You, and You have set his bounds so that he cannot pass;

title: Job 14:6
text: look away from him, so that he may rest until he shall finish his day, as a hireling.

title: Job 14:7
text: For there is hope of a tree, if it is cut down, that it will sprout again, and its tender branch will not cease.

title: Job 14:8
text: Though its root becomes old in the earth, and its stump dies in the dust,

title: Job 14:9
text: [yet] at the scent of water it will bud and bring forth branches like a plant.

title: Job 14:10
text: But man dies and is cut off; and man expires, and where [is] he?

title: Job 14:11
text: [As] the waters fail from the sea, and a river falls away and dries up,

title: Job 14:12
text: so man lies down and does not rise. Till the heavens [are] no more, they shall not awake, nor be awakened out of their sleep.

title: Job 14:13
text: Who will grant [that] You would hide me in the grave, that You would keep me secret, until Your wrath is past, that You would set me a fixed time and remember me?

title: Job 14:14
text: If a man die, shall he revive? All the days of my warfare I will wait, until my change comes.

title: Job 14:15
text: You shall call, and I will answer You; You shall have a desire to the work of Your hands.

title: Job 14:16
text: For now You number my steps; do You not watch over my sin?

title: Job 14:17
text: My transgression [is] sealed up in a bag, and You cover over my iniquity.

title: Job 14:18
text: And surely a falling mountain crumbles away, and the rock moves out of its place.

title: Job 14:19
text: The waters wear away the stones; the outpouring of it washes the dust of the earth; and You cause the hope of man to perish.

title: Job 14:20
text: You overpower him forever, and he passes; You change his face, and send him away.

title: Job 14:21
text: His sons come to honor, and he knows it not; they fall, but he does not mark [it].

title: Job 14:22
text: But his flesh is pained within him; and his soul mourns over him.

title: Job 15:1
text: And Eliphaz the Temanite answered and said,

title: Job 15:2
text: [Should] a wise man answer with windy knowledge, and fill his belly with the east wind?

title: Job 15:3
text: Should he reason with talk [that is] not useful, or with speeches which have no profit?

title: Job 15:4
text: Yea, you do away with fear, and take away prayer before God.

title: Job 15:5
text: For your iniquity teaches your mouth, and you choose the tongue of the crafty.

title: Job 15:6
text: Your own mouth condemns you, and not I; yes, your own lips testify against you.

title: Job 15:7
text: [Were] you the first man born? Or were you made before the hills?

title: Job 15:8
text: Have you heard the secret counsel of God? And do you limit wisdom to yourself?

title: Job 15:9
text: What do you know that we do not know, or understand that is not with us?

title: Job 15:10
text: With us [are] both the gray-headed and aged, mightier than your father [as to] days.

title: Job 15:11
text: [Are] the comforts of God small with you, and a word [dealing] gently with you?

title: Job 15:12
text: Why does your heart carry you away? And what do your eyes wink at,

title: Job 15:13
text: that you turn your spirit against God, and let [such] words go out of your mouth?

title: Job 15:14
text: What [is] man, that he should be clean? And [what is he] born of a woman that he should be righteous?

title: Job 15:15
text: Behold, He puts no trust in His saints; yea, the heavens are not clean in His sight.

title: Job 15:16
text: How much more hateful and filthy [is] man, who drinks iniquity like water?

title: Job 15:17
text: I will show you; hear me; and what I have seen I will declare,

title: Job 15:18
text: that which wise men have told, and have not hidden from their fathers;

title: Job 15:19
text: to them alone the earth was given, and no stranger passed among them.

title: Job 15:20
text: The wicked man labors in pain all his days, and the number of years is hidden for the ruthless one.

title: Job 15:21
text: A dreadful sound of things [is] in his ears; the destroyer shall come to him in peace.

title: Job 15:22
text: He does not believe in a return from darkness, but he [is] awaited by the sword.

title: Job 15:23
text: He wanders for bread, saying, Where [is it]? He knows that the day of darkness is ready at hand.

title: Job 15:24
text: Trouble and pain shall terrify him; they shall overpower him, as a king ready for the battle;

title: Job 15:25
text: because he stretches out his hand against God, and sets himself against the Almighty.

title: Job 15:26
text: He runs at him, with a [stiff] neck, with the thick layers of his shields,

title: Job 15:27
text: because he has covered his face with fat; he has put fat on [his] loins.

title: Job 15:28
text: And he lives [in] cut off cities, [in] houses where none [are] living, which are ready [to become] heaps.

title: Job 15:29
text: He shall not be rich, nor shall his wealth hold out, nor shall he stretch out his gain on the earth.

title: Job 15:30
text: He shall not escape from darkness; the flame shall dry up his branches, and at the breath of his mouth he shall turn away.

title: Job 15:31
text: Let not [he] being deceived trust in vanity; for vanity shall be his reward.

title: Job 15:32
text: It shall be done before his time, and his branch shall not be green.

title: Job 15:33
text: He shall shake off its unripe grape, as the vine; and shall cast off his flower like the olive.

title: Job 15:34
text: For the company of the ungodly [shall be] barren, and fire shall devour the tents of bribery.

title: Job 15:35
text: They conceive mischief, and bring forth evil, and their belly prepares deceit.

title: Job 16:1
text: And Job answered and said,

title: Job 16:2
text: I have heard many such [things]. You [are] all miserable comforters.

title: Job 16:3
text: [Shall] words of wind [have] an end? Or what provokes you that you should answer?

title: Job 16:4
text: I also could speak as you [do]; if your soul were in my soul's place. I could heap up words against you, and shake my head at you.

title: Job 16:5
text: I might make you strong with my mouth, and the moving of my lips would spare you.

title: Job 16:6
text: Though I speak, my pain is not held back, and [though] I forbear, in what way am I eased?

title: Job 16:7
text: But now He has made me weary; You have made all my company desolate.

title: Job 16:8
text: And You have plucked me, for it is a witness, and my failure rises up against me, and it answers to my face.

title: Job 16:9
text: His anger has torn and hated [me]; He gnashes on me with His teeth; my enemy sharpens his eyes at me;

title: Job 16:10
text: They have gaped on me with their mouth; and have scornfully beaten me on the cheek; they gather themselves against me.

title: Job 16:11
text: God has delivered me to the perverse; and turned me over into the hands of the wicked.

title: Job 16:12
text: I was at ease, but He has broken me in pieces; yea, [He has] also taken [me] by my neck and shaken me to pieces and set me up for His mark.

title: Job 16:13
text: His archers hem me in; He splits my inward parts, and does not spare; He pours out my gall on the ground.

title: Job 16:14
text: He breaks me with break on break; He runs on me like a giant.

title: Job 16:15
text: I have sewed sackcloth on my skin and thrust my horn in the dust.

title: Job 16:16
text: My face is reddened from weeping, and on my eyelids [is] the shadow of death;

title: Job 16:17
text: though no violence [is] in my hand, and my prayer [is] pure.

title: Job 16:18
text: Oh earth, do not cover my blood, and let not my cry have a place.

title: Job 16:19
text: Also now, behold, my Witness [is] in Heaven, and He who testifies of me [is] on high.

title: Job 16:20
text: My friends scorn me; my eye pours out [tears] to God.

title: Job 16:21
text: Oh that one might plead for a man with God, as a man [pleads] for his neighbor!

title: Job 16:22
text: For the years [that are few] will come, and I shall go the way from where I shall not return.

title: Job 17:1
text: My spirit is broken, my days are ended, the graves [are] ready for me.

title: Job 17:2
text: [Are] not mockeries with me? Yea, my eye rests on their insults.

title: Job 17:3
text: Please lay down a pledge for me with Yourself; who [is] he [who] will strike hands with me?

title: Job 17:4
text: For You have hidden their heart from understanding; therefore You shall not lift [them] up.

title: Job 17:5
text: He who for a share informs [against] friends, even the eyes of his children shall fail.

title: Job 17:6
text: He has made me also a byword of the peoples; and I am one in whose face they spit.

title: Job 17:7
text: My eye also is dim from grief; and all my members [are] like a shadow.

title: Job 17:8
text: Upright ones shall be amazed at this, and the innocent shall stir himself up against the ungodly.

title: Job 17:9
text: The righteous also shall hold [on] his way, and he who has clean hands adds strength.

title: Job 17:10
text: And now all of them, go back, and please come again; and I shall not find among you a wise man.

title: Job 17:11
text: My days are past, my purposes [are] broken off, the desires of my heart.

title: Job 17:12
text: They set night for day; the light [is] near in the face of darkness.

title: Job 17:13
text: If I wait for the grave [as] my home, I have made my bed in the darkness;

title: Job 17:14
text: I have said to corruption, You [are] my father; to the worm, My mother and my sister!

title: Job 17:15
text: And where then [is] my hope? And [as for] my hope, who shall see it?

title: Job 17:16
text: They shall go down [to] the bars of the pit, when [our] descent together [is] in the dust.

title: Job 18:1
text: And Bildad the Shuhite answered and said,

title: Job 18:2
text: Until when will you set a snare for words? Understand, and afterwards we will speak.

title: Job 18:3
text: Why are we counted as cattle, or seem stupid in your sight?

title: Job 18:4
text: He tears himself in his anger; [shall] the earth [be] forsaken for you? And shall the rock be moved out of its place?

title: Job 18:5
text: Yes, the light of the wicked shall be put out, and the spark of his fire shall not shine.

title: Job 18:6
text: The light shall be dark in his tent, and his lamp shall be put out with him.

title: Job 18:7
text: The steps of his strength shall be hampered, and his own plans shall throw him down.

title: Job 18:8
text: For he is thrown into a net by his own feet, and he walks on a net.

title: Job 18:9
text: The trap shall take [him] by the heel, and the noose shall hold sway over him.

title: Job 18:10
text: The pitfall [is] laid for him in the ground, and a trap for him in the way.

title: Job 18:11
text: Terrors shall make him afraid on every side, and shall dash him at his feet.

title: Job 18:12
text: His strength shall be hunger-bitten, and trouble shall be ready at his side.

title: Job 18:13
text: It shall devour the parts of his skin; the first-born of death consumes his parts.

title: Job 18:14
text: His hope shall be rooted out of his tent, and you marched to the king of terrors.

title: Job 18:15
text: What [is] not his shall dwell in his tent; brimstone shall be scattered on his home.

title: Job 18:16
text: His roots shall be dried up beneath, and his branch shall wither above.

title: Job 18:17
text: His memory shall perish from the earth, and there is no name to him on the face of the street.

title: Job 18:18
text: They drive him from light to darkness, and they make him flee from the world.

title: Job 18:19
text: He shall have neither son nor kinsman among his people, nor [any] remaining in his dwellings.

title: Job 18:20
text: Those after him shall be amazed at his day; and those before were seized [with] horror.

title: Job 18:21
text: Surely these [are] the dwellings of the perverse, and this the place [that] has not known God.

title: Job 19:1
text: And Job answered and said,

title: Job 19:2
text: How long will you torment my soul and break me in pieces with words?

title: Job 19:3
text: [And] this, ten times you have blamed me; you are not ashamed that you have wronged me.

title: Job 19:4
text: And [if] indeed I have erred, my error remains with me.

title: Job 19:5
text: If indeed you magnify yourself against me, and plead against me my misery,

title: Job 19:6
text: know now that God has overthrown me, and His net has closed on me.

title: Job 19:7
text: Behold, I cry out, Violence! And I am not answered. I cry aloud, but there is no justice.

title: Job 19:8
