text: The house of the wicked shall be overthrown, but the tent of the upright shall be blessed.

title: Proverbs 14:12
text: There is a way which seems right to a man, but the end of it [is] the ways of death.

title: Proverbs 14:13
text: Even in laughter the heart is sorrowful, and the end of that joy [is] heaviness.

title: Proverbs 14:14
text: The backslider in heart shall be filled with his own ways, but a good man from himself.

title: Proverbs 14:15
text: The simple believes every word, but the wise man watches his step.

title: Proverbs 14:16
text: A wise one fears and departs from evil, but the fool rages and is sure.

title: Proverbs 14:17
text: He who [is] soon angry acts foolishly, and a man of wicked plots is hated.

title: Proverbs 14:18
text: The simple inherit folly, but the wise are crowned with knowledge.

title: Proverbs 14:19
text: The evil bow before the good, and the wicked at the gates of the righteous.

title: Proverbs 14:20
text: The poor is hated even by his own neighbor, but the rich [has] many friends.

title: Proverbs 14:21
text: He who despises his neighbor sins, but he who has mercy on the poor, happy [is] he.

title: Proverbs 14:22
text: Do not those who think evil go astray? But mercy and truth shall be to those who think of good.

title: Proverbs 14:23
text: In all labor there is gain, but the talk of the lips [tends] only to poverty.

title: Proverbs 14:24
text: The crown of the wise [is] their riches [of wisdom]; the foolishness of fools [is] folly.

title: Proverbs 14:25
text: A true witness delivers souls, but a deceitful witness speaks lies.

title: Proverbs 14:26
text: In the fear of the LORD [is] strong hope, and His sons shall have a place of refuge.

title: Proverbs 14:27
text: The fear of the LORD [is] a fountain of life to turn aside from the snares of death.

title: Proverbs 14:28
text: In the multitude of people [is] the king's honor, but in the lack of people [is] the ruin of the prince.

title: Proverbs 14:29
text: [He who is] slow to wrath [is] of great understanding, but [he who is] hasty of spirit exalts folly.

title: Proverbs 14:30
text: A sound heart [is] the life of the flesh, but envy the rottenness of the bones.

title: Proverbs 14:31
text: He who presses the poor curses his Maker, but he who honors Him has mercy upon the poor.

title: Proverbs 14:32
text: The wicked is driven away in his wickedness, but the righteous [has] hope in his death.

title: Proverbs 14:33
text: Wisdom rests in the heart of him who has understanding, but among fools it is made known.

title: Proverbs 14:34
text: Righteousness lifts up a nation, but sin [is] a shame to any people.

title: Proverbs 14:35
text: The king's favor [is] toward a wise servant, but his wrath is against him who causes shame.

title: Proverbs 15:1
text: A soft answer turns away wrath, but grievous words stir up anger.

title: Proverbs 15:2
text: The tongue of the wise uses knowledge rightly, but the mouth of fools pours out foolishness.

title: Proverbs 15:3
text: The eyes of the LORD [are] in every place, beholding the evil and the good.

title: Proverbs 15:4
text: A wholesome tongue [is] a tree of life, but crookedness in it [is] a break in the spirit.

title: Proverbs 15:5
text: A fool despises his father's instruction, but he who listens to correction is wise.

title: Proverbs 15:6
text: In the house of the righteous [is] much treasure, but in the gain of the wicked [is] trouble.

title: Proverbs 15:7
text: The lips of the righteous send forth knowledge, but the heart of the foolish [is] not so.

title: Proverbs 15:8
text: The sacrifice of the wicked [is] a hateful thing to the LORD, but the prayer of the upright [is] His delight.

title: Proverbs 15:9
text: The way of the wicked [is] hateful to the LORD, but He loves him who pursues righteousness.

title: Proverbs 15:10
text: Correction [is] grievous to him who forsakes the way; he who hates reproof shall die.

title: Proverbs 15:11
text: Hell and destruction [are] before the LORD; even more the hearts of the sons of men?

title: Proverbs 15:12
text: A scorner does not love one who corrects him, nor will he go to the wise.

title: Proverbs 15:13
text: A merry heart makes a cheerful face, but by sorrow of heart the spirit is broken.

title: Proverbs 15:14
text: The heart of him who has understanding seeks knowledge, but the mouth of fools feeds on foolishness.

title: Proverbs 15:15
text: All the days of the afflicted [are] evil, but gladness of heart is a continual a feast.

title: Proverbs 15:16
text: Better [is] a little with the fear of the LORD than great treasure and tumult with it.

title: Proverbs 15:17
text: Better [is] a dinner of vegetables where love is, than a stalled ox and hatred with it.

title: Proverbs 15:18
text: A wrathful man stirs up fighting, but one slow to anger calms fighting.

title: Proverbs 15:19
text: The way of the lazy one [is] like a hedge of thorns, but the way of the righteous [is] made plain.

title: Proverbs 15:20
text: A wise son makes a glad father, but a foolish man despises his mother.

title: Proverbs 15:21
text: Folly [is] joy to him who is without any wisdom, but a man of understanding walks uprightly.

title: Proverbs 15:22
text: Without wisdom, purposes are defeated, but by many wise men they are established.

title: Proverbs 15:23
text: A man [has] joy by the answer of his mouth, and a word in due season, how good [it is]!

title: Proverbs 15:24
text: The way of life [is] above to the wise, so that he may turn away from hell below.

title: Proverbs 15:25
text: The LORD will destroy the house of the proud, but He will set up the border of the widow.

title: Proverbs 15:26
text: The thoughts of the wicked [are] very hateful to the LORD, but the words of the pure [are] pleasant words.

title: Proverbs 15:27
text: He who is greedy for gain troubles his own house, but he who hates bribes shall live.

title: Proverbs 15:28
text: The heart of the righteous studies to answer, but the mouth of the wicked pours out evil things.

title: Proverbs 15:29
text: The LORD [is] far from the wicked, but He hears the prayer of the righteous.

title: Proverbs 15:30
text: The light of the eyes rejoices the heart; a good report makes the bones fat.

title: Proverbs 15:31
text: The ear that hears the reproof of life shall remain among the wise.

title: Proverbs 15:32
text: He who refuses instruction despises his own soul, but he who hears reproof gets understanding.

title: Proverbs 15:33
text: The fear of the LORD [is] the instruction of wisdom, and before honor [is] humility.

title: Proverbs 16:1
text: The ordering of the heart in man, and the answer of the tongue, [is] from the LORD.

title: Proverbs 16:2
text: All the ways of a man [are] clean in his own eyes, but the LORD weighs the spirits.

title: Proverbs 16:3
text: Roll your works upon the LORD, and your thoughts shall be established.

title: Proverbs 16:4
text: The LORD has made all for His purpose; yea, even the wicked for the day of evil.

title: Proverbs 16:5
text: Everyone proud in heart [is] hateful to the LORD; though hand [join] in hand, he shall not be unpunished.

title: Proverbs 16:6
text: By mercy and truth, iniquity is purged, and by the fear of the LORD [men] turn away from evil.

title: Proverbs 16:7
text: When a man's ways please the LORD, He makes even his enemies to be at peace with him.

title: Proverbs 16:8
text: Better [is] a little with righteousness than great gain without right.

title: Proverbs 16:9
text: A man's heart plans his way, but the LORD directs his steps.

title: Proverbs 16:10
text: A divine sentence [is] in the lips of the king; his mouth does not transgress in judgment.

title: Proverbs 16:11
text: A just weight and balance [are] the LORD's; all the weights of the bag [are] His work.

title: Proverbs 16:12
text: [It is] a hateful thing for kings to commit wickedness; for the throne [is] established by righteousness.

title: Proverbs 16:13
text: Righteous lips [are] the delight of kings, and they love him who speaks right.

title: Proverbs 16:14
text: The wrath of a king [is as] messengers of death, but a wise man will quiet it.

title: Proverbs 16:15
text: In the light of the king's face [is] life, and his favor [is] like a cloud of the latter rain.

title: Proverbs 16:16
text: How much better [it is] to get wisdom than gold! And to get understanding is rather to be chosen than silver!

title: Proverbs 16:17
text: The way of the upright [is] to turn away from evil; he who keeps his way guards his way.

title: Proverbs 16:18
text: Pride goes before destruction, and a haughty spirit before a fall.

title: Proverbs 16:19
text: [It is] better [to be] of an humble spirit with the lowly than to divide the spoil with the proud.

title: Proverbs 16:20
text: He who handles a matter wisely shall find good, and whoever trusts in the LORD, happy [is] he.

title: Proverbs 16:21
text: The wise in heart shall be called prudent, and the sweetness of the lips increases learning.

title: Proverbs 16:22
text: Understanding [is] a fountain of life to him who has it, but the instruction of fools [is] folly.

title: Proverbs 16:23
text: The heart of the wise teaches his mouth, and adds learning to his lips.

title: Proverbs 16:24
text: Pleasant words [are like] a honeycomb, sweet to the soul, and health to the bones.

title: Proverbs 16:25
text: There is a way [that seems] right to a man, but the end of it [is] the ways of death.

title: Proverbs 16:26
text: He who labors works for himself, for his mouth craves it from him.

title: Proverbs 16:27
text: An ungodly man plots evil, and his lips [are] like a burning fire.

title: Proverbs 16:28
text: A perverse man causes fighting, and a whisperer separates chief friends.

title: Proverbs 16:29
text: A violent man lures his neighbor and makes him go in a way not good.

title: Proverbs 16:30
text: He shuts his eyes to think of perverse things; moving his lips, he brings evil to pass.

title: Proverbs 16:31
text: The gray head [is] a crown of glory, [if] it is found in the way of righteousness.

title: Proverbs 16:32
text: He who is slow to anger [is] better than the mighty, and he who rules his spirit is better than he who takes a city.

title: Proverbs 16:33
text: The lot is cast into the lap, but the whole disposing of it [is] from the LORD.

title: Proverbs 17:1
text: Better [is] a dry piece of bread, and quietness with it, than a house full of sacrifices [with] fighting.

title: Proverbs 17:2
text: A wise servant shall have rule over a son who causes shame, and shall have part of the inheritance among the brothers.

title: Proverbs 17:3
text: The refining pot [is] for silver, and the furnace for gold, but the LORD tries the hearts.

title: Proverbs 17:4
text: A wicked doer gives heed to false lips; a liar gives ear to an evil tongue.

title: Proverbs 17:5
text: Whoever scorns the poor reviles his Maker; he who is glad at calamities shall not be unpunished.

title: Proverbs 17:6
text: Sons of sons [are] the crown of old men, and the glory of sons [are] their fathers.

title: Proverbs 17:7
text: An excellent lip [is] not fitting for a fool; much less are lying lips fitting for a prince.

title: Proverbs 17:8
text: A bribe [is] like a precious stone in the eyes of him who has it; wherever he turns, he is prudent.

title: Proverbs 17:9
text: He who covers a transgression seeks love, but he who repeats a matter separates friends.

title: Proverbs 17:10
text: A reproof enters more into a wise man than a thousand stripes into a fool.

title: Proverbs 17:11
text: An evil one seeks only rebellion; so a cruel messenger shall be sent against him.

title: Proverbs 17:12
text: Let a bear robbed [of her cubs] meet a man, rather than a fool in his folly.

title: Proverbs 17:13
text: Whoever rewards evil for good, evil shall not depart from his house.

title: Proverbs 17:14
text: The beginning of strife [is like] letting out water; therefore leave off fighting, before it breaks out.

title: Proverbs 17:15
text: He who justifies the wicked, and he who condemns the just, even both of them [are] hateful to the LORD.

title: Proverbs 17:16
text: Why [is there] a price in the hand of a fool to get wisdom, since [he has] no heart [for it]?

title: Proverbs 17:17
text: A friend loves at all times, and a brother is born for the time of trouble.

title: Proverbs 17:18
text: A man lacking heart strikes hands; he pledges in the presence of his friend.

title: Proverbs 17:19
text: He who loves fighting loves transgression; he who makes his gate high seeks ruin.

title: Proverbs 17:20
text: He who has a perverse heart finds no good, and he who [has] a crooked tongue falls into mischief.

title: Proverbs 17:21
text: He who fathers a fool [does it] to his sorrow; the father of a fool has no joy.

title: Proverbs 17:22
text: A merry heart does good [like] a medicine, but a broken spirit dries the bones.

title: Proverbs 17:23
text: A wicked [man] takes a bribe out of the bosom to pervert the ways of judgment.

title: Proverbs 17:24
text: Wisdom [is] before him who has understanding, but the eyes of a fool [are] in the ends of the earth.

title: Proverbs 17:25
text: A foolish son [is] a grief to his father, and bitterness to her who bore him.

title: Proverbs 17:26
text: And [it is] not good to punish the just, nor to strike princes for uprightness.

title: Proverbs 17:27
text: He who has knowledge uses few words; a man of understanding is of an excellent spirit.

title: Proverbs 17:28
text: Even a fool, when he [is] silent, is counted wise, and he who shuts his lips [is counted as] a man of understanding.

title: Proverbs 18:1
text: He that separates himself seeks [his own] desire; he breaks out against all sound wisdom.

title: Proverbs 18:2
text: A fool has no delight in understanding, but only that his heart may lay itself bare.

title: Proverbs 18:3
text: When the wicked comes, scorn also comes, and with shame comes reproach.

title: Proverbs 18:4
text: The words of a man's mouth are like deep waters; the fountain of wisdom [is like] a flowing stream.

title: Proverbs 18:5
text: [It is] not good to favor the person of the wicked, [nor] to overthrow the righteous in judgment.

title: Proverbs 18:6
text: A fool's lips enter into argument, and his mouth calls for strokes.

title: Proverbs 18:7
text: A fool's mouth [is] his destruction, and his lips [are] the snare of his soul.

title: Proverbs 18:8
text: The words of a talebearer [are] as wounds, and they go down into the innermost parts of the belly.

title: Proverbs 18:9
text: Also he who is slack in his work is brother to a great destroyer.

title: Proverbs 18:10
text: The name of the LORD [is] a strong tower; the righteous man runs into it and is safe.

title: Proverbs 18:11
text: The rich man's wealth [is] his strong city, and as a high wall in his own mind.

title: Proverbs 18:12
text: Before shattering, the heart of man is proud, and before honor [is] humility.

title: Proverbs 18:13
text: If one answers a matter before he hears, it [is] folly and shame to him.

title: Proverbs 18:14
text: The spirit of a man will nourish his sickness, but a wounded spirit who can bear?

title: Proverbs 18:15
text: The heart of the prudent gets knowledge, and the ear of the wise seeks knowledge.

title: Proverbs 18:16
text: A man's gift makes room for him, and brings him before great men.

title: Proverbs 18:17
text: The first in his cause [seems] just, [but] his neighbor comes and searches him.

title: Proverbs 18:18
text: The lot causes arguments to cease, and divides between the mighty.

title: Proverbs 18:19
text: An brother offended [is like] a strong city; and [their] disagreements [are] like the bars of a fortress.

title: Proverbs 18:20
text: A man's belly shall be satisfied with the fruit of his mouth; he shall be satisfied with the product of his lips.

title: Proverbs 18:21
text: Death and life [are] in the power of the tongue, and those who love it shall eat the fruit of it.

title: Proverbs 18:22
text: [Whoever] finds a wife finds good and gets favor from the LORD.

title: Proverbs 18:23
text: The poor speaks humble requests, but the rich answers roughly.

title: Proverbs 18:24
text: A man who has friends may be broken up, but there is a Lover who sticks closer than a brother.

title: Proverbs 19:1
text: Better [is] the poor who walks in his integrity than he who [is] perverse in his lips, and is a fool.

title: Proverbs 19:2
text: Also without knowledge the soul [is] not good, and he who hurries with his feet sins.

title: Proverbs 19:3
text: The foolishness of man perverts his way, and his heart frets against the LORD.

title: Proverbs 19:4
text: Wealth makes many friends; but the poor is separated from his neighbor.

title: Proverbs 19:5
text: A false witness shall not be unpunished, and a breather of lies shall not escape.

title: Proverbs 19:6
text: Many will beg the favor of a ruler, and all [are] friends to a man who gives gifts.

title: Proverbs 19:7
text: All the brothers of the poor man hate him; how much more do his friends go far from him? He pursues [them] with words, yet they [are] lacking.

title: Proverbs 19:8
text: He who gets wisdom loves his own soul; he who keeps understanding shall find good.

title: Proverbs 19:9
text: A false witness shall not be unpunished, and one speaking lies shall perish.

title: Proverbs 19:10
text: Luxury is not becoming for a fool; much less for a servant to have rule over princes.

title: Proverbs 19:11
text: The judgment of a man puts off his anger; and [it is] his glory to pass over a transgression.

title: Proverbs 19:12
text: The king's wrath [is] like the roaring of a lion; but his favor [is] like dew on the grass.

title: Proverbs 19:13
text: A foolish son [is] ruin to his father, and the quarreling of a wife [is] a never-ending dripping.

title: Proverbs 19:14
text: Houses and riches [are] the inheritance of fathers, and a prudent wife [is] from the LORD.

title: Proverbs 19:15
text: Laziness throws one into a deep sleep, and an idle soul shall suffer hunger.

title: Proverbs 19:16
text: He who keeps the commandment keeps his own soul; he who despises His ways shall die.

title: Proverbs 19:17
text: He who has pity upon the poor lends to the LORD, and He will reward his dealing to him.

title: Proverbs 19:18
text: Chasten your son while there is hope, and do not set your soul on making him die.

title: Proverbs 19:19
text: A man of great wrath shall suffer punishment; for if you deliver [him] yet you must do it again.

title: Proverbs 19:20
text: Hear advice, and receive instruction, so that you may be wise in your latter end.

title: Proverbs 19:21
text: [There are] many purposes in a man's heart, but the counsel of the LORD shall stand.

title: Proverbs 19:22
text: The charm of a man [is] his kindness, and a poor man [is] better than a liar.

title: Proverbs 19:23
text: The fear of the LORD [tends] to life, and he rests satisfied; he shall not be visited with evil.

title: Proverbs 19:24
text: A lazy one puts his hand in a dish, and he will not return it to his mouth.

title: Proverbs 19:25
text: Strike a scorner, and the simple will beware; reprove one who has understanding, and he will understand knowledge.

title: Proverbs 19:26
text: He who assaults his father [and] chases away his mother [is] a son who causes shame and brings reproach.

title: Proverbs 19:27
text: My son, cease to hear the discipline, [only] to stray from the words of knowledge.

title: Proverbs 19:28
text: An ungodly witness scorns judgment, and the mouth of the wicked devours iniquity.

title: Proverbs 19:29
text: Judgments are prepared for scorners, and stripes for the back of fools.

title: Proverbs 20:1
text: Wine [is] a mocker, strong drink [is] raging, and whoever goes astray by it [is] not wise.

title: Proverbs 20:2
text: The fear of a king [is] as the roaring of a lion; whoever stirs him up to anger sins against his own soul.

title: Proverbs 20:3
text: [It is] an honor for a man to cease from strife, but every fool exposes himself.

title: Proverbs 20:4
text: The lazy one will not plow; after the autumn he shall beg in harvest and have nothing.

title: Proverbs 20:5
text: Wisdom in the heart of man [is like] deep water, but a man of understanding will draw it out.

title: Proverbs 20:6
text: Most men will proclaim each his own goodness, but a faithful man who can find?

title: Proverbs 20:7
text: The just walks in his integrity; his sons [are] blessed after him.

title: Proverbs 20:8
text: A king who sits in the throne of judgment scatters away all evil with his eyes.

title: Proverbs 20:9
text: Who can say, I have made my heart clean; I am pure from my sin?

title: Proverbs 20:10
text: Different kinds of weights, different kinds of measures, both [are] hateful to the LORD.

title: Proverbs 20:11
text: Even a child is known by his own doings, whether his work [is] pure and whether [it is] right.

title: Proverbs 20:12
text: The hearing ear and the seeing eye, the LORD has made both of them.

title: Proverbs 20:13
text: Do not love sleep, lest you come to poverty; open your eyes and you shall be satisfied with bread.

title: Proverbs 20:14
text: [It is] bad! Bad, says the buyer; but when [it is] left to him, then he boasts.

title: Proverbs 20:15
text: There is gold and a multitude of rubies; but the lips of knowledge [are] a rare jewel.

title: Proverbs 20:16
text: Take the garment of him who is surety [for] a stranger; and take a pledge from him for strangers.

title: Proverbs 20:17
text: Bread of deceit [is] sweet to a man, but afterwards his mouth shall be filled with gravel.

title: Proverbs 20:18
text: Purposes are established by counsel; and with good advice make war.

title: Proverbs 20:19
text: A gossip is a revealer of secrets; so do not mix with him who flatters with his lips.

title: Proverbs 20:20
text: Whoever curses his father or his mother, his lamp shall be put out in deep darkness.

title: Proverbs 20:21
text: An inheritance gotten hastily in the beginning, even the end of it shall not be blessed.

title: Proverbs 20:22
text: Do not say, I will repay evil; wait on the LORD, and He will save you.

title: Proverbs 20:23
text: Different kinds of weights [are] hateful to the LORD, and a false balance [is] not good.

title: Proverbs 20:24
text: Man's steps [are] of the LORD; how can a man then understand his own way?

title: Proverbs 20:25
text: [It is] a snare [to] a man to say rashly, A holy thing, and afterward vows to ask [about it].

title: Proverbs 20:26
text: A wise king scatters the wicked and brings the wheel over them.

title: Proverbs 20:27
text: The spirit of man [is] the lamp of the LORD, searching all the inward parts of the belly.

title: Proverbs 20:28
text: Mercy and truth preserve the king; and his throne is upheld by mercy.

title: Proverbs 20:29
text: The glory of young men [is] their strength; and the beauty of old men [is] the gray head.

title: Proverbs 20:30
text: The stripes of a wound cleanses away evil, and strokes the inward parts of the belly.

title: Proverbs 21:1
text: The king's heart [is] in the hand of the LORD [as] the rivers of water; He turns it wherever He will.

title: Proverbs 21:2
text: Every way of a man [is] right in his own eyes, but the LORD ponders the hearts.

title: Proverbs 21:3
text: To do justice and judgment [is] more pleasing to the LORD than sacrifice.

title: Proverbs 21:4
text: A high look, a proud heart, [and] the plowing of the wicked, [is] sin.

title: Proverbs 21:5
text: The thoughts of the diligent [tend] only to plenty; but the thoughts of everyone [who is] hasty only to poverty.

title: Proverbs 21:6
text: The getting of treasures by a lying tongue [is] a vanity tossed to and fro by those who seek death.

title: Proverbs 21:7
text: The robbery of the wicked shall destroy them, because they refuse to do judgment.

title: Proverbs 21:8
text: The way of a guilty man [is] perverted; but the pure, his work [is] right.

title: Proverbs 21:9
text: [It is] better to dwell in a corner of the housetop than [with] a quarrelsome woman and to share a house.

title: Proverbs 21:10
text: The soul of the wicked desires evil; his neighbor finds no favor in his eyes.

title: Proverbs 21:11
text: When the scorner is punished, the simple is made wise; and when the wise is instructed, he receives knowledge.

title: Proverbs 21:12
text: The righteous wisely considers the house of the wicked; [but God] overthrows the wicked for [their] wickedness.

title: Proverbs 21:13
text: Whoever stops his ears at the cry of the poor, he also shall cry himself, but shall not be heard.

title: Proverbs 21:14
text: A gift in secret quiets anger; and a bribe in the bosom quiets strong wrath.

title: Proverbs 21:15
text: [It is] joy to the just to do judgment, but ruin [shall be] to the workers of iniquity.

title: Proverbs 21:16
text: The man who wanders out of the way of understanding shall rest in the assembly of departed spirits.

title: Proverbs 21:17
text: He who loves pleasure [shall be] a poor man; he who loves wine and oil shall not be rich.

title: Proverbs 21:18
text: The wicked [shall be] a ransom for the righteous, and the transgressor for the upright.

title: Proverbs 21:19
text: [It is] better to dwell in the wilderness than with a quarrelsome and angry woman.

title: Proverbs 21:20
text: A desirable treasure and oil [are] in the home of the wise; but a foolish man swallows it up.

title: Proverbs 21:21
text: He who follows after righteousness and mercy finds life, righteousness, and honor.

title: Proverbs 21:22
text: A wise one scales the city of the mighty and brings down the strength of its hope.

title: Proverbs 21:23
text: Whoever keeps his mouth and his tongue keeps his soul from troubles.

title: Proverbs 21:24
text: Proud, haughty scorner [is] his name, he who deals in proud wrath.

title: Proverbs 21:25
text: The desire of the lazy man kills him, for his hands have refused to work.

title: Proverbs 21:26
text: He covets greedily all the day long; but the righteous gives and spares not.

title: Proverbs 21:27
text: The sacrifice of the wicked [is] hateful to God; how much more [when] he brings it with a wicked mind?

title: Proverbs 21:28
text: A false witness shall perish, but the man who hears speaks on and on.

title: Proverbs 21:29
text: A wicked man hardens his face, but the upright establishes his way.

title: Proverbs 21:30
text: [There is] no wisdom nor understanding nor counsel against the LORD.

title: Proverbs 21:31
text: The horse [is] prepared for the day of battle; but safety [is] from the LORD.

title: Proverbs 22:1
text: A [good] name [is] rather to be chosen than great riches; [and] loving favor rather than silver or gold.

title: Proverbs 22:2
text: The rich and poor meet together; the LORD [is] the maker of them all.

title: Proverbs 22:3
text: A prudent one foresees the evil and hides himself, but the simple pass on and are punished.

title: Proverbs 22:4
text: By humility [and] the fear of the LORD [are] riches and honor and life.

title: Proverbs 22:5
text: Thorns [and] snares [are] in the way of the perverse; he who keeps his soul shall be far from them.

title: Proverbs 22:6
text: Train up a child in the way he should go; and when he is old, he will not depart from it.

title: Proverbs 22:7
text: The rich rules over the poor, and the borrower [is] servant to the lender.

title: Proverbs 22:8
text: He who sows iniquity shall reap vanity; and the rod of his anger shall fail.

title: Proverbs 22:9
text: He who has a bountiful eye shall be blessed; for he gives of his bread to the poor.

title: Proverbs 22:10
text: Cast out the scorner, and fighting shall go out; yes, quarrels and shame shall cease.

title: Proverbs 22:11
text: He who loves pureness of heart, grace is on his lips; the king [shall be] his friend.

title: Proverbs 22:12
text: The eyes of the LORD keep knowledge, and He overthrows the words of the transgressor.

title: Proverbs 22:13
text: The lazy one says, [There is] a lion outside; I shall be killed in the streets.

title: Proverbs 22:14
text: The mouth of strange women [is] a deep pit; those despised [by] the LORD shall fall there.

title: Proverbs 22:15
text: Foolishness [is] bound in the heart of a child; the rod of correction shall drive it far from him.

title: Proverbs 22:16
text: He who crushes the poor to multiply for himself, and he who gives to the rich, only [to come] to poverty.

title: Proverbs 22:17
text: Bow down your ear, and hear the words of the wise, and apply your heart to My knowledge.

title: Proverbs 22:18
text: For [it is] a pleasant thing if you keep them within you; they shall all be fitted in your lips,

title: Proverbs 22:19
text: so that your trust may be in the LORD, I have made known to you this day, even to you.

title: Proverbs 22:20
text: Have I not written to you excellent things in counsels and knowledge,

title: Proverbs 22:21
text: that I might make you know the sureness of the words of truth; to return the words of truth to those who send to you?

title: Proverbs 22:22
text: Do not rob the poor, because he [is] poor; nor press down the afflicted in the gate;

title: Proverbs 22:23
text: for the LORD will plead their cause, and strip the soul of those who plunder them.

title: Proverbs 22:24
text: Make no friendship with an angry man; and you shall not go up with a man of fury,

title: Proverbs 22:25
text: lest you learn his ways and get a snare to your soul.

title: Proverbs 22:26
text: Be not one of those who strike hands, of those who are sureties for debts.

title: Proverbs 22:27
text: If you have nothing to pay, why should he take away your bed from under you?

title: Proverbs 22:28
text: Do not remove the old landmark which your fathers have set.

title: Proverbs 22:29
text: Do you see a man diligent in his business? He shall stand before kings; he shall not stand before unknown [men].

title: Proverbs 23:1
text: When you sit down to eat with a ruler, look carefully at what [is] before you;

title: Proverbs 23:2
text: and put a knife to your throat, if you [are] a man given to appetite.

title: Proverbs 23:3
text: Do not desire his delicacies, for they [are] deceitful food.

title: Proverbs 23:4
text: Do not labor to be rich; cease from your own understanding.

title: Proverbs 23:5
text: Will your eyes fly on it? And [it] is gone! For surely it makes wings for itself; it flies [into] the heavens like an eagle.

title: Proverbs 23:6
text: Do not eat the bread of [him who has] an evil eye, nor desire his dainty foods;

title: Proverbs 23:7
text: for as he thinks in his heart, so [is] he; Eat and drink, he says to you, but his heart [is] not with you.

title: Proverbs 23:8
text: Your bit [which] you have eaten, you shall vomit up, and spoil your pleasant words.

title: Proverbs 23:9
text: Do not speak in the ears of a fool, for he will despise the wisdom of your words.

title: Proverbs 23:10
text: Do not remove the old landmarks, and do not enter into the fields of the fatherless;

title: Proverbs 23:11
text: for their Redeemer [is] mighty; He shall plead their cause with you.

title: Proverbs 23:12
text: Apply your heart to instruction and your ears to the words of knowledge.

title: Proverbs 23:13
text: Do not withhold correction from a boy, for [if] you beat him with the rod, he will not die.

title: Proverbs 23:14
text: You shall beat him with the rod, and shall deliver his soul from hell.

title: Proverbs 23:15
text: My son, if your heart is wise, my heart shall rejoice, even mine.

title: Proverbs 23:16
text: Yea, my heart shall rejoice when your lips speak right things.

title: Proverbs 23:17
text: Do not let your heart envy sinners; but [be] in the fear of the LORD all the day long.

title: Proverbs 23:18
text: For surely there is a hereafter, and your hope shall not be cut off.

title: Proverbs 23:19
text: My son, hear and be wise, and guide your heart in the way.

title: Proverbs 23:20
text: Do not be among those who drink much wine, among gluttons for flesh for themselves,

title: Proverbs 23:21
text: for the drunkard and the glutton lose all, and sleepiness shall clothe [a man] with rags.

title: Proverbs 23:22
text: Listen to your father who sired you, and do not despise your mother when she is old.

title: Proverbs 23:23
text: Buy the truth, and sell [it] not; also wisdom, and instruction, and understanding.

title: Proverbs 23:24
text: The father of the righteous shall greatly rejoice; and he who fathers a wise [child] shall have joy from him.

title: Proverbs 23:25
text: Your father and your mother shall be glad, and she who bore you shall rejoice.

title: Proverbs 23:26
text: My son, give Me your heart, and let your eyes watch My ways.

title: Proverbs 23:27
text: For a harlot [is] a deep ditch, and a strange woman [is] a narrow pit.

title: Proverbs 23:28
text: She also lies in wait as [for] prey, and increases the treacherous among men.

title: Proverbs 23:29
text: Who [has] woe? Who has sorrow? Who [has] fighting? Who [has] babbling? Who has wounds without cause? Who has redness of eyes?

title: Proverbs 23:30
text: Those who stay long at the wine, those who go to seek mixed wine.

title: Proverbs 23:31
text: Do not look upon the wine when it is red, [when] it gives its color in the cup, [when] it goes down smoothly

title: Proverbs 23:32
text: At the last it bites like an asp and stings like an adder.

title: Proverbs 23:33
text: Your eyes shall look upon strange women and your heart shall speak perverse things.

title: Proverbs 23:34
text: Yes, you shall be as one who lies down in the middle of the sea, or as one who lies upon the top of a mast,

title: Proverbs 23:35
text: [saying], They struck me; I was not sick; they beat me, [but] I did not know it. When I awaken, I will add [more]. I will seek it again.

title: Proverbs 24:1
text: Do not be jealous of evil men, nor desire to be with them.

title: Proverbs 24:2
text: For their heart studies ruin, and their lips talk of mischief.

title: Proverbs 24:3
text: Through wisdom a house is built, and by understanding it is established;

title: Proverbs 24:4
text: and by knowledge the rooms shall be filled with all precious and pleasant riches.

title: Proverbs 24:5
text: A wise man [is] strong; yes, a man of knowledge increases strength.

title: Proverbs 24:6
text: For by wise counsel you shall make your war; and in a multitude of wise men [there is] safety.

title: Proverbs 24:7
text: Wisdom [is] too high for a fool; he does not open his mouth in the gate.

title: Proverbs 24:8
text: He who plots to do evil shall be called a master of wicked thoughts.

title: Proverbs 24:9
text: The thought of foolishness [is] sin; and the scorner [is] hateful to men.

title: Proverbs 24:10
text: [If] you faint in the day of trial, your strength [is] small.

title: Proverbs 24:11
text: Deliver those being taken to death, and those stumbling to be killed, unless you hold back.

title: Proverbs 24:12
text: if you say, Behold, we did not know; does not He who searches the heart consider it? And the Keeper of your soul, does He know? And He repays to a man according to his works?

title: Proverbs 24:13
text: My son, eat honey, because [it is] good; and the honeycomb, [is] sweet to your palate;

title: Proverbs 24:14
text: so [shall] the knowledge of wisdom [be] to your soul; when you have found it, then there shall be a reward, and your hope shall not be cut off.

title: Proverbs 24:15
text: Wicked one, do not lie in ambush at the dwelling of the righteous; do not spoil his resting place;

title: Proverbs 24:16
text: for a just one falls seven times, and rises up again; but the wicked shall fall into evil.

title: Proverbs 24:17
text: Do not rejoice when your enemy falls, and do not let your heart be glad when he stumbles;

title: Proverbs 24:18
text: lest the LORD see, and it displease Him, and He turn away His wrath from him.

title: Proverbs 24:19
text: Do not fret yourself because of evil ones, nor be jealous of the wicked;

title: Proverbs 24:20
text: for there shall be not be a hereafter to the evil; the lamp of the wicked shall be put out.

title: Proverbs 24:21
text: My son, fear the LORD and the king; [and] do not fellowship with those who are given to change;

title: Proverbs 24:22
text: for their trouble shall rise suddenly, and who knows the ruin of them both?

title: Proverbs 24:23
text: These also [are] for the wise: To have respect of persons in judgment [is] not good.

title: Proverbs 24:24
text: He who says to the wicked, You [are] righteous; the people shall curse him [and] nations shall abhor him.

title: Proverbs 24:25
text: But to those who rebuke [him], it shall be a delight, and a good blessing shall come upon them.

title: Proverbs 24:26
text: He shall kiss the lips that return right words.

title: Proverbs 24:27
text: Prepare your work outside, and make it fit for yourself in the field; and afterwards build your house.

title: Proverbs 24:28
text: Do not be a witness against your neighbor without cause, nor deceive with your lips.

title: Proverbs 24:29
text: Do not `say, I will do so to him as he has done to me; I will give to the man according to his work.

title: Proverbs 24:30
text: I went by the field of the lazy man, and by the vineyard of the man without understanding;

title: Proverbs 24:31
text: and, lo, it was all grown over with thorns, [and] nettles had covered the face of it, and its stone wall was broken down.

title: Proverbs 24:32
text: Then I saw; I set my heart on it; I looked and I received instruction.

title: Proverbs 24:33
text: A little sleep, a little slumber, a little folding of the hands to lie down;

title: Proverbs 24:34
text: then your poverty comes stalking, and your want like an a man [armed with] a shield.

title: Proverbs 25:1
text: These [are] also proverbs of Solomon which the men of Hezekiah king of Judah copied out.

title: Proverbs 25:2
text: The glory of God [is] to hide a thing; but the honor of kings [is] to search out a matter.

title: Proverbs 25:3
text: The heavens for height, and the earth for depth, but the heart of kings [is] without searching.

title: Proverbs 25:4
text: Take away the dross from the silver, and there shall come forth a vessel for the refiner.

title: Proverbs 25:5
text: Take away the wicked [from] before the king, and his throne shall be founded in righteousness.

title: Proverbs 25:6
text: Do not put yourself forth in the presence of the king, and do not stand in the place of the great;

title: Proverbs 25:7
text: for [it is] better that it should be said to you, Come up here, than that you should be put lower in the presence of a noble whom your eyes have seen.

title: Proverbs 25:8
text: Do not go forth quickly to fight, lest [you know not] what to do in the end of it, when your neighbor has put you to shame.

title: Proverbs 25:9
text: Debate your cause with your neighbor; and do not uncover a secret to another,

title: Proverbs 25:10
text: lest he who hears [it] put you to shame, and your evil report turn not away.

title: Proverbs 25:11
text: A word fitly spoken [is like] apples of gold in pictures of silver.

title: Proverbs 25:12
text: [As] a ring of gold, and an ornament of fine gold, [so is] a wise reprover upon a hearing ear.

title: Proverbs 25:13
text: Like cold snow in the time of harvest, [so is] a faithful messenger to his senders; [for] he makes return [to] his master's soul.

title: Proverbs 25:14
text: A man boasting himself in a false gift [is like] clouds and wind, but no rain.

title: Proverbs 25:15
text: In [being] slow to anger a ruler is won over, and a soft tongue breaks the bone.

title: Proverbs 25:16
text: Have you found honey? Eat [only] as much as is enough for you, lest you be filled with it and vomit it.

title: Proverbs 25:17
text: Withdraw your foot from your neighbor's house, lest he be weary of you and hate you.

title: Proverbs 25:18
text: A man who bears false witness against his neighbor [is] a maul, and a sword, and a sharp arrow.

title: Proverbs 25:19
text: Trust in an unfaithful man in time of trouble [is like] a broken tooth, and a foot out of joint.

title: Proverbs 25:20
text: [As] he who takes away a garment in cold weather, [as] vinegar upon niter, [so is] he who sings songs to a heavy heart.

title: Proverbs 25:21
text: If your enemy is hungry, give him bread to eat; and if he is thirsty, give him water to drink,

title: Proverbs 25:22
text: for you shall heap coals [of fire] upon his head, and the LORD shall reward you.

title: Proverbs 25:23
text: The north wind drives away rain; so [does] an angry face a backbiting tongue.

title: Proverbs 25:24
text: [It is] better to dwell in the corner of the housetop than with a quarreling woman and to share a house.

title: Proverbs 25:25
text: [Like] cold waters to a thirsty soul, [so is] good news from a far country.

title: Proverbs 25:26
text: A righteous man falling down before the wicked [is like] a troubled fountain and a rotten spring.

title: Proverbs 25:27
text: [It is] not good to eat much honey; so [for men] to search their own glory [is not] glory.

title: Proverbs 25:28
text: He who [has] no rule over his own spirit [is like a] broken down city without a wall.

title: Proverbs 26:1
text: As snow in summer, and as rain in harvest, so honor [is] not becoming for a fool.

title: Proverbs 26:2
text: As the bird by wandering, as the swallow by flying, so the curse without cause shall not come.

title: Proverbs 26:3
text: A whip for the horse, a bridle for the ass, and a rod for the fool's back.

title: Proverbs 26:4
text: Do not answer a fool according to his foolishness, lest you also be like him.

title: Proverbs 26:5
text: Answer a fool according to his foolishness, so that he may not be wise in his own eyes.

title: Proverbs 26:6
text: He who sends a message by the hand of a fool cuts off the feet [and] drinks down damage.

title: Proverbs 26:7
text: The legs of the lame [are] not equal; so [is] a parable in the mouth of fools.

title: Proverbs 26:8
text: As he who binds a stone in a sling, so [is] he who gives honor to a fool.

title: Proverbs 26:9
text: [As] a thorn goes up into the hand of a drunkard, so [is] a parable in the mouth of fools.

title: Proverbs 26:10
text: Great [is] the Former of all, but he who hires a fool [is like] one who hires one passing by.

title: Proverbs 26:11
text: As a dog returns to its vomit, [so] a fool returns to his folly.

title: Proverbs 26:12
text: Do you see a man wise in his own eyes? [There is] more hope for a fool than for him.

title: Proverbs 26:13
text: The lazy one says, [There is] a lion in the way; a lion [is] in the streets.

title: Proverbs 26:14
text: [As] the door turns upon its hinges, [so does] the lazy man turn upon his bed.

title: Proverbs 26:15
text: The lazy man hides his hand in [his] bosom; it grieves him to bring it again to his mouth.

title: Proverbs 26:16
text: The sluggard [is] wiser in his own eyes than seven men who can give a reason.

title: Proverbs 26:17
text: He who passes by enraging himself over strife not his own [is like] one who takes a dog by the ears,

title: Proverbs 26:18
text: [or] like a madman who throws firebrands, arrows, and death.

title: Proverbs 26:19
text: so [is] the man who deceives his neighbor and says, Am I not joking.

title: Proverbs 26:20
text: Where there is no wood, the fire goes out; and where [there is] no talebearer, the fighting ceases.

title: Proverbs 26:21
text: [As] coals to burning coals, and wood to fire, so [is] a quarrelsome man to kindle fighting.

title: Proverbs 26:22
text: The words of a talebearer [are] as wounds, and they go down into the innermost parts of the belly.

title: Proverbs 26:23
text: Burning lips and a wicked heart [are like] a broken piece of pottery with silver waste.

title: Proverbs 26:24
text: He who hates pretends with his lips and stores up deceit within him.

title: Proverbs 26:25
text: When he makes his voice gracious, do not believe him; for seven hateful things [are] in his heart.

title: Proverbs 26:26
text: [He whose] hatred is covered by deceit, his wickedness shall be shown before the congregation.

title: Proverbs 26:27
text: Whoever digs a pit shall fall into it; and he who rolls a stone, it will return on him.

title: Proverbs 26:28
text: A lying tongue hates [those] afflicted by it, and a flattering mouth works ruin.

title: Proverbs 27:1
text: Do not boast yourself of tomorrow, for you do not know what a day may bring forth.

title: Proverbs 27:2
text: Let another man praise you, and not your mouth; a stranger, and not your lips.

title: Proverbs 27:3
text: A stone [is] heavy, and sand [is] heavy; but a fool's wrath [is] heavier than them both.

title: Proverbs 27:4
text: Wrath [is] cruel, and anger [is] overwhelming; but who [is] able to stand before envy?

title: Proverbs 27:5
text: Open rebuke [is] better than secret love.

title: Proverbs 27:6
text: Faithful [are] the wounds of a friend; but the kisses of an enemy [are] deceitful.

title: Proverbs 27:7
text: The full soul despises a honeycomb; but to the hungry soul every bitter thing [is] sweet.

title: Proverbs 27:8
text: As a bird that wanders from her nest, so [is] a man who wanders from his place.

title: Proverbs 27:9
text: Ointment and perfume rejoice the heart; so does the sweetness of one's friend by advice from the heart.

title: Proverbs 27:10
text: Your own friend, and your father's friend, do not forsake them; nor go to your brother's house in the day of your trouble; better [is] a neighbor that is near than a brother far off.

title: Proverbs 27:11
text: My son, be wise, and make my heart glad, so that I may answer him who shames me.

title: Proverbs 27:12
text: A sensible one foresees the evil [and] hides himself, but the simple pass on [and] are punished.

title: Proverbs 27:13
text: Take his robe that is surety for a stranger, and take a pledge from him for a strange woman.

title: Proverbs 27:14
text: He who blesses his friend with a loud voice, rising early in the morning, it shall be counted a curse to him.

title: Proverbs 27:15
text: A never-ending dropping in a very rainy day and a quarrelsome woman are alike.

title: Proverbs 27:16
text: Whoever hides her hides the wind, and his right [hand] encounters [slippery] oil.

title: Proverbs 27:17
text: Iron sharpens iron, so a man sharpens the face of his friend.

title: Proverbs 27:18
text: Whoever keeps the fig tree shall eat its fruit; so he who waits on his master shall be honored.

title: Proverbs 27:19
text: As in water face [answers] to face, so the heart of man [answers] to man.

title: Proverbs 27:20
text: Hell and destruction are never full; so the eyes of man are never satisfied.

title: Proverbs 27:21
text: [As] the refining pot for silver and the furnace for gold, so [is] a man to his praise.

title: Proverbs 27:22
text: Though you should pound a fool in a bowl with a bar in the midst of wheat, his foolishness will not depart from him.

title: Proverbs 27:23
text: Know well the face of your flocks; set your heart on your herds.

title: Proverbs 27:24
text: For riches [are] not forever; nor the crown from generation to generation?

title: Proverbs 27:25
text: When the hay is removed, and the tender grass is seen, and mountain-plants are gathered,

title: Proverbs 27:26
text: the lambs [are] for your clothing, and the goats [are] the price of the field.

title: Proverbs 27:27
text: And [you shall have] goats' milk enough for your food, for the food of your household, and a living for your young women.

title: Proverbs 28:1
text: The wicked flee [when] no man pursues; but the righteous are bold as a lion.

title: Proverbs 28:2
text: Because of the transgression of a land, many [are] its rulers; but [it is] prolonged by a man of discernment who knows [right].

title: Proverbs 28:3
text: A poor man who crushes the poor [is like] a sweeping rain which leaves no food.

title: Proverbs 28:4
text: Those who forsake the law praise the wicked; but those who keep the law plead against them.

title: Proverbs 28:5
text: Evil men do not understand judgment; but those who seek the LORD understand all [things].

title: Proverbs 28:6
text: Better [is] the poor who walks in his uprightness than he who [is] perverse [in his] ways, though he [is] rich.

title: Proverbs 28:7
text: Whoever keeps the law [is] a wise son, but a companion of gluttons shames his father.

title: Proverbs 28:8
text: He who increases his wealth by interest and unjust gain, [he shall] gather it for him who will pity the poor.

title: Proverbs 28:9
text: He who turns away his ear from hearing the law, even his prayer [is] a hateful thing.

title: Proverbs 28:10
text: Whoever causes the righteous man to go astray in an evil way, he himself shall fall into his own pit; but the upright shall inherit good.

title: Proverbs 28:11
text: The rich man [is] wise in his own eyes; but the poor who has understanding searches him out.

title: Proverbs 28:12
text: When the righteous rejoice, [there is] great glory; but when the wicked rise, a man is hidden.

title: Proverbs 28:13
text: He who covers his sins shall not be blessed; but whoever confesses and leaves [them] shall have mercy.

title: Proverbs 28:14
text: Blessed [is] the man dreading [God], but he who hardens his heart shall fall into mischief.

title: Proverbs 28:15
text: [Like] a roaring lion and a ranging bear, [so is] a wicked ruler over the helpless people.

title: Proverbs 28:16
text: A ruler lacking understanding even adds oppressions; he who hates unjust gain shall prolong [his] days.

title: Proverbs 28:17
text: A man who is pressed down with the blood of a soul shall flee to the pit; do not let them uphold him.

title: Proverbs 28:18
text: Whoever walks uprightly shall be saved; but he who is perverse [in his] ways shall fall at once.

title: Proverbs 28:19
text: He who tills his land shall have plenty of bread, but he pursuing vanities shall have poverty enough.

title: Proverbs 28:20
text: A faithful man shall overflow with blessings, but he who makes haste to be rich shall not be innocent.

title: Proverbs 28:21
text: To have respect of persons [is] not good; yea, for a piece of bread a man will transgress.

title: Proverbs 28:22
text: He who hastens to be rich [has] an evil eye, and does not know that poverty will come upon him.

title: Proverbs 28:23
text: He who rebukes a man shall afterwards find [more] favor than he who flatters [with] the tongue.

title: Proverbs 28:24
text: Whoever robs his father or his mother and says, [It is] no sin he [shall be] a companion to a destroyer.

title: Proverbs 28:25
text: He who is of a proud heart stirs up fighting; but he who puts his trust in the LORD shall be made fat.

title: Proverbs 28:26
text: He who trusts in his own heart is a fool; but whoever walks wisely, he shall be delivered.

title: Proverbs 28:27
text: He who gives to the poor shall not lack, but he who hides his eyes shall have many a curse.

title: Proverbs 28:28
text: When the wicked rise, a man hides himself, but when they perish, the righteous increase.

title: Proverbs 29:1
text: A man who hardens [his] neck [when] reproved shall be suddenly broken, and there will be no healing.

title: Proverbs 29:2
text: When the righteous increase, the people rejoice; but when the wicked rule, the people mourn.

title: Proverbs 29:3
text: Whoever loves wisdom rejoices his father; but a companion of harlots wastes wealth.

title: Proverbs 29:4
text: The king establishes the land by judgment; but he [taking] bribes tears it down.

title: Proverbs 29:5
text: A man who flatters his neighbor spreads a net for his feet.

title: Proverbs 29:6
text: In the sin of an evil man [there is] a snare; but the righteous sings and rejoices.

title: Proverbs 29:7
text: The righteous knows the plea of the poor; the wicked cares not to know it.

title: Proverbs 29:8
text: Scornful men bring a city into a snare, but the wise turn away wrath.

title: Proverbs 29:9
text: [If] a wise man contends with a foolish man, whether he rages or laughs, [there is] no rest.

title: Proverbs 29:10
text: Men of blood hate the upright; but the just seek his soul.

title: Proverbs 29:11
text: A fool speaks all his mind; but a wise one keeps it in until afterwards.

title: Proverbs 29:12
text: If a ruler listens to lies, all his servants [are] wicked.

title: Proverbs 29:13
text: The poor and the deceitful man meet together; the LORD gives light to the eyes of both.

title: Proverbs 29:14
text: A king who truly judges the weak, his throne shall be established forever.

title: Proverbs 29:15
text: The rod and rebuke give wisdom, but a boy sent off causes shame to his mother.

title: Proverbs 29:16
text: When the wicked are multiplied, sin increases; but the righteous shall see their fall.

title: Proverbs 29:17
text: Correct your son, and he shall give you rest; yea, he shall give delight to your soul.

title: Proverbs 29:18
text: Where [there is] no wisdom, the people perish; but he who keeps the law, he [is] blessed.

title: Proverbs 29:19
text: A servant will not be corrected by words, for though he understands, he will not answer.

title: Proverbs 29:20
text: Do you see a man hasty in his words? [There is] more hope for a fool than for him.

title: Proverbs 29:21
text: He pampering his servant from youth, [that one] in his after days shall [his] successor.

title: Proverbs 29:22
text: An angry man stirs up fighting, and a furious man abounds in sin.

title: Proverbs 29:23
text: A man's pride shall bring him low; but honor shall uphold the humble in spirit.

title: Proverbs 29:24
text: He who shares with a thief hates his own soul; he hears an oath and does not tell.

title: Proverbs 29:25
text: The fear of man brings a snare, but whoever puts his trust in the LORD shall be safe.

title: Proverbs 29:26
text: Many seek the ruler's favor; but each man's judgment [comes] from the LORD.

title: Proverbs 29:27
text: An unjust man [is] a hateful thing to the just; and [he who is] upright in the way [is] hateful to the wicked.

title: Proverbs 30:1
text: The words of Agur the son of Jakeh, the prophecy: The man spoke to Ithiel, to Ithiel and Ucal, saying,

title: Proverbs 30:2
text: Surely I [am more] like an animal than any man, and do not have the understanding of a man.

title: Proverbs 30:3
text: I have not learned wisdom, nor the knowledge of the holy.

title: Proverbs 30:4
text: Who has gone up [to] Heaven and has come down? Who has gathered the wind in His fists? Who has bound the waters in [His] garments? Who has established all the ends of the earth? What [is] His name, and what [is] His Son's name? Surely you know.

title: Proverbs 30:5
text: Every word of God [is] pure; He [is] a shield to those who put their trust in Him.

title: Proverbs 30:6
text: Do not add to His words, lest He reprove you and you be found a liar.

title: Proverbs 30:7
text: I have asked two things from You; do not deny them before I die;

title: Proverbs 30:8
text: remove far from me vanity and a lying word; give me neither poverty or riches; tear for me my portion of bread,

title: Proverbs 30:9
text: lest I be full and deceive, and say, Who [is] the LORD? Or lest I be poor, and steal, and violate the name of my God.

title: Proverbs 30:10
text: Do not accuse a servant to his master, lest he curse you, and you be found guilty.

title: Proverbs 30:11
text: [There is] a generation that curses their father, and does not bless their mother.

title: Proverbs 30:12
text: [There is] a generation [that are] pure in their own eyes, and yet is not washed from their own filth.

title: Proverbs 30:13
text: [There is] a generation, O how lofty are their eyes! And their eyelids are lifted up.

title: Proverbs 30:14
text: [There is] a generation whose teeth are like swords, and their jaw teeth like knives, to devour the poor from off the earth, and the needy from [among] men.

title: Proverbs 30:15
text: The leech [has] two daughters, [crying], Give, give! Three things are never satisfied, yea, four things never say, Enough!

title: Proverbs 30:16
text: The grave; and the barren womb, the earth not filled [with] water, and the fire, have not said, Enough.

title: Proverbs 30:17
text: The eye [that] mocks at [his] father and despises to obey [his] mother, the ravens of the valley shall pick it out, and the young eagles shall eat it.

title: Proverbs 30:18
text: Three [things are] too wonderful for me, yea, four which I do not know:

title: Proverbs 30:19
text: the way of an eagle in the air; the way of a snake on a rock; the way of a ship in the middle of the sea; and the way of a man with a maiden.

title: Proverbs 30:20
text: Such [is] the way of an adulterous woman; she eats, and wipes her mouth, and says, I have done no evil.

title: Proverbs 30:21
text: Under three [things] the earth quakes, and under four it is not able to bear up:

title: Proverbs 30:22
text: for a servant when he reigns; and a fool when he is filled with food;

title: Proverbs 30:23
text: for a hateful woman when she is married; and a servant girl that is heir to her mistress.

title: Proverbs 30:24
text: Four [things are] little on the earth, but they [are] exceedingly wise:

title: Proverbs 30:25
text: the ants [are] a people not strong, yet they prepare their food in the summer;

title: Proverbs 30:26
text: the rock-badgers [are] not a mighty people, yet they make their houses in the rock;

title: Proverbs 30:27
text: the locusts have no king, yet they go forth by bands, all of them;

title: Proverbs 30:28
text: you can take the lizard with the hands, yet it [is] in king's palaces.

title: Proverbs 30:29
text: There [are] three [things] which go well in a march, yea, four that go well in walking:

title: Proverbs 30:30
text: a lion [is] mighty among beasts and does not turn away for any;

title: Proverbs 30:31
text: one girded in the loins; and a he-goat; and a king [when his] army [is] with him.

title: Proverbs 30:32
text: If you have done foolishly in lifting yourself up, or if you have thought evil, [lay your] hand on your mouth.

title: Proverbs 30:33
text: Surely the churning of milk brings forth butter, and the wringing of the nose brings forth blood; so the forcing of wrath brings forth fighting.

title: Proverbs 31:1
text: The words of king Lemuel, the prophecy which his mother taught him.

title: Proverbs 31:2
text: What, my son? And what, the son of my womb? And what, the son of my vows?

title: Proverbs 31:3
text: Do not give your strength to women, nor your ways to that which destroys kings.

title: Proverbs 31:4
text: [It is] not for kings, O Lemuel, not for kings to drink wine; nor for princes [to lust] for strong drink;

title: Proverbs 31:5
text: lest they drink, and forget the law, and pervert the judgment of any of the afflicted.

title: Proverbs 31:6
text: Give strong drink to him who is ready to perish, and wine to those who are of heavy hearts.

title: Proverbs 31:7
text: Let him drink, and forget his poverty, and remember his misery no more.

title: Proverbs 31:8
text: Open your mouth for the dumb, for the cause of all the sons [of those] passing away.

title: Proverbs 31:9
text: Open your mouth, judge righteously, and plead the cause of the poor and needy.

title: Proverbs 31:10
text: Who can find a woman of virtue? For her value [is] far above rubies.

title: Proverbs 31:11
text: The heart of her husband trusts safely in her, so that he shall have no need of plunder.

title: Proverbs 31:12
text: She will do him good and not evil all the days of her life.

title: Proverbs 31:13
text: She seeks wool and flax, and works willingly [with] her hands.

title: Proverbs 31:14
text: She is like the merchants' ships; she brings her food from afar.

title: Proverbs 31:15
text: She also rises while [it is] still night, and gives food to her household, and a share to her young women.

title: Proverbs 31:16
text: She considers a field, and buys it; with the fruit of her hands she plants a vineyard.

title: Proverbs 31:17
text: She binds her loins with strength, and makes her arms strong.

title: Proverbs 31:18
text: She sees that her merchandise [is] good; her lamp does not go out by night.

title: Proverbs 31:19
text: She lays her hands to the spindle, and her hands hold the distaff.

title: Proverbs 31:20
text: She stretches out her hand to the poor; yea, she reaches forth her hands to the needy.

title: Proverbs 31:21
text: She is not afraid of the snow for her household; for all her household [are] clothed [with] scarlet.

title: Proverbs 31:22
text: She makes herself coverings; her clothing [is] silk and purple.

title: Proverbs 31:23
text: Her husband is known in the gates, when he sits among the elders of the land.

title: Proverbs 31:24
text: She makes fine linen and sells [it], and delivers girdles to the merchants.

title: Proverbs 31:25
text: Strength and honor [are] her clothing; and she shall rejoice in time to come.

title: Proverbs 31:26
text: She opens her mouth with wisdom; and in her tongue [is] the law of kindness.

title: Proverbs 31:27
text: She looks well to the ways of her household, and does not eat the bread of idleness.

title: Proverbs 31:28
text: Her sons rise up and call her blessed; her husband [also], and he praises her.

title: Proverbs 31:29
text: Many daughters have done well, but you excel them all.

title: Proverbs 31:30
text: Favor [is] deceitful, and beauty [is] vain, [but] a woman who fears the LORD, she shall be praised.

title: Proverbs 31:31
text: Give her of the fruit of her hands; and let her own works praise her in the gates.

title: Ecclesiastes 1:1
text: The words of the Preacher, the son of David, king in Jerusalem.

title: Ecclesiastes 1:2
text: Vanity of vanities, says the Preacher, vanity of vanities! all [is] vanity.

title: Ecclesiastes 1:3
text: What [is] the profit to a man in all his labor which he labors under the sun?

title: Ecclesiastes 1:4
text: A generation passes away, and a generation comes; but the earth remains forever.

title: Ecclesiastes 1:5
text: The sun also arises, and the sun goes down, and hurries to its place where it arose.

title: Ecclesiastes 1:6
text: The wind goes toward the south, and it turns around to the north; it whirls around continually; and the wind returns on its circuits.

title: Ecclesiastes 1:7
text: All the rivers run into the sea; yet the sea [is] not full; to the place from where the rivers come, there they return again.

title: Ecclesiastes 1:8
text: All things [are] full of labor; man cannot utter it; the eye is not satisfied with seeing, nor the ear filled with hearing.

title: Ecclesiastes 1:9
text: That which has been [is] that which shall be; and that which has been done [is] that which shall be done; and [there is] nothing new under the sun.

title: Ecclesiastes 1:10
text: Is there a thing [of] which it may be said, See, this [is] new? It has already been in days of old, which were before us.

title: Ecclesiastes 1:11
text: [There is] no memory of former [things], and also of after [things] when he shall be; for neither shall be a remembrance of them with those who will be at the afterwards.

title: Ecclesiastes 1:12
text: I the Preacher was king over Israel in Jerusalem.

title: Ecclesiastes 1:13
text: And I gave my heart to seek and search out by wisdom concerning all which is done under the heavens. [It is] a sad task God has given to the sons of men to be humbled by it.

title: Ecclesiastes 1:14
text: I have seen all the works that are done under the sun; and, behold, all [is] vanity and vexation of spirit.

title: Ecclesiastes 1:15
text: What [is] crooked cannot be made straight; and [that] lacking cannot be numbered.

title: Ecclesiastes 1:16
text: I spoke within my own heart, saying, Lo, I have become great and have gathered more wisdom than all that have been before me in Jerusalem; yea, my heart has seen much of wisdom and knowledge.

title: Ecclesiastes 1:17
text: And I gave my heart to know wisdom and to know madness and folly; I know that this also [is] vexation of spirit.

title: Ecclesiastes 1:18
text: For in much wisdom [is] much grief; and he who increases knowledge increases sorrow.

title: Ecclesiastes 2:1
text: I said in my heart, Come now, I will test you with mirth; therefore consider and behold goodness; this also [is] vanity.

title: Ecclesiastes 2:2
text: I said of laughter, [It is] madness; and of mirth, What does it do?

title: Ecclesiastes 2:3
text: I sought in my heart to drag my flesh with wine, yet leading my heart with wisdom; and to lay hold on folly, until I might see where the good for the sons of men might be, what they should do under the heavens all the days of their life.

title: Ecclesiastes 2:4
text: I made my works great; I built houses for myself; I planted vineyards for myself.

title: Ecclesiastes 2:5
text: I made gardens and orchards for myself, And I planted trees in them, of all fruit.

title: Ecclesiastes 2:6
text: I made pools of water for myself, to water the forest shooting forth trees.

title: Ecclesiastes 2:7
text: I bought slaves and slave women, and sons of the house were mine; also livestock, a herd and a great flock were mine, above all that were before me in Jerusalem.

title: Ecclesiastes 2:8
text: I also gathered silver and gold to myself, and the treasure of kings and of the provinces. I got men singers and women singers for myself, and the delights of the sons of men, a wife and very many wives.

title: Ecclesiastes 2:9
text: I was great and increased more than all that were before me in Jerusalem; also my wisdom remained with me.

title: Ecclesiastes 2:10
text: And whatever my eyes desired I did not keep from them; I did not withhold my heart from any joy; for my heart rejoiced in all my labor, and this was my part of all my labor.

title: Ecclesiastes 2:11
text: Then I looked on all the works that my hands had done, and on the labor that I had labored to do; and, behold, all [is] vanity and vexation of spirit; and [there is] no profit under the sun.

title: Ecclesiastes 2:12
text: And I turned to behold wisdom, and madness, and folly; for what [can] the man [do] who comes after the king, when they have already done it?

title: Ecclesiastes 2:13
text: Then I saw that wisdom excels folly, as far as light excels darkness.

title: Ecclesiastes 2:14
text: The wise man's eyes [are] in his head; but the fool walks in darkness; and I also knew that one event happens to all of them.

title: Ecclesiastes 2:15
text: Then I said in my heart, As it happens to the fool, [so] it happens even to me; and why was I then more wise? And I said in my heart that this also [is] vanity.

title: Ecclesiastes 2:16
text: For [there is] no memory of the wise [more than] of the fool forever, since that which is now shall all be forgotten in the days to come. And how does the wise die above the fool!

title: Ecclesiastes 2:17
text: Therefore I hated life; because the work that is done under the sun [is] sad to me; for all [is] vanity and vexation of spirit.

title: Ecclesiastes 2:18
text: Yes, I hated all my labor which I had done under the sun; that I must leave it to the man who shall be after me.

title: Ecclesiastes 2:19
text: And who knows [whether] he shall be wise or a fool? Yet he shall have rule over all my labor in which I have labored, and acted wisely under the sun. This [is] also vanity.

title: Ecclesiastes 2:20
text: And I turned to cause my heart to despair over all the labor which I did under the sun.

title: Ecclesiastes 2:21
text: When there is a man whose labor is in wisdom, and in knowledge, and with success; yet to a man who has not labored in it, he shall leave it [for] his share. This also is vanity and a great evil.

title: Ecclesiastes 2:22
text: For what has man from all his labor, and from the troubling of his heart, in which he has labored under the sun?

title: Ecclesiastes 2:23
text: For all his days [are] sorrows, and his labor sadness; yea, his heart does not take rest in the night. This [is] also vanity.

title: Ecclesiastes 2:24
text: Is it not good that he should eat and drink and make his soul see good in his labor? This I also saw, that it [was] from the hand of God.

title: Ecclesiastes 2:25
text: For who can eat, or who can enjoy, apart from me?

title: Ecclesiastes 2:26
text: For [God] gives wisdom, and knowledge, and joy to a man who [is] good in His sight. But to the sinner He gives labor, to gather and to heap up, that he may give to [him who is] good before God. This also [is] vanity and vexation of spirit.

title: Ecclesiastes 3:1
text: To every thing [there is] a season, and a time for every purpose under the heavens:

title: Ecclesiastes 3:2
text: a time to be born, and a time to die; a time to plant, and a time to pull up what [is] planted;

title: Ecclesiastes 3:3
text: a time to kill, and a time to heal; a time to break down, and a time to build up;

title: Ecclesiastes 3:4
text: a time to weep, and a time to laugh; a time to mourn, and a time to dance;

title: Ecclesiastes 3:5
text: a time to throw away stones, and a time to gather stones together; a time to embrace, and a time to refrain from embracing;

title: Ecclesiastes 3:6
text: a time to get, and a time to lose; a time to keep, and a time to throw away;

title: Ecclesiastes 3:7
text: a time to tear, and a time to sew; a time to keep silence, and a time to speak;

title: Ecclesiastes 3:8
text: a time to love, and a time to hate; a time of war, and a time of peace.

title: Ecclesiastes 3:9
text: What profit does he have who works in that in which he labors?

title: Ecclesiastes 3:10
text: I have seen the task which God has given to the sons of men to be humbled by it.

title: Ecclesiastes 3:11
text: He has made everything beautiful in His time; also He has set eternity in their heart, so that no man can find out the work that God makes from the beginning to the end.

title: Ecclesiastes 3:12
text: I know that [there is] no good in them, but to rejoice and to do good in his life.

title: Ecclesiastes 3:13
text: And also that every man should eat and drink, and enjoy the good of all his labor, it [is] the gift of God.

title: Ecclesiastes 3:14
text: I know that whatever God does, it shall be forever; nothing can be added to it, nor anything taken from it; and God does [it] so that they fear before Him.

title: Ecclesiastes 3:15
text: That which has been is now; and that which [is] to be has already been; and God requires that which is past.

title: Ecclesiastes 3:16
text: And again I saw under the sun the place of judgment, that wickedness [was] there; and the place of righteousness, that wickedness [was] there.

title: Ecclesiastes 3:17
text: I said in my heart, God shall judge the righteous and the wicked; for [there is] a time there for every purpose and for every work.

title: Ecclesiastes 3:18
text: I said in my heart concerning the matter of sons of men, that God might reveal them, and that they might see that they themselves [are] beasts.

title: Ecclesiastes 3:19
text: For that which happens [to] the sons of men also happens to beasts even one thing [happens] to them. As this [one] dies, so that [one] dies; yea, they all [have] one breath; so that a man has no advantage over a beast; for all [is] vanity.

title: Ecclesiastes 3:20
text: All go to one place; all are of the dust, and all return to dust again.

title: Ecclesiastes 3:21
text: Who knows the spirit of man [that] goes upward, and the spirit of the beast [that] goes downward?

title: Ecclesiastes 3:22
text: Therefore I have seen that [there is] nothing better than that a man should rejoice in his own works; for that [is] his portion; for who can bring him to see what shall be after him?

title: Ecclesiastes 4:1
text: So I returned, and considered all the oppressions that are done under the sun. And behold the tears of the oppressed ones, and hey had no comforter! And on the side of those who oppressed them there [was] power, but they had no comforter.

title: Ecclesiastes 4:2
text: And I commended the dead who already have died, more than the living who [are] living now.

title: Ecclesiastes 4:3
text: Yea, better than both [is he] who has not yet been, who has not seen the evil work that is done under the sun.

title: Ecclesiastes 4:4
text: Again, I considered all labor, and every right work, that for this a man is envied by his neighbor. This [is] also vanity and vexation of spirit.

title: Ecclesiastes 4:5
text: The fool folds his hands together, and eats his own flesh.

title: Ecclesiastes 4:6
text: Better [is] a hand filled with rest than two fists [with] travail and vexation of spirit.

title: Ecclesiastes 4:7
text: And I returned and saw vanity under the sun.

title: Ecclesiastes 4:8
text: There is one [alone], and [there is] not a second; yea, he has neither son nor brother; yet there is no end to all his labor; and his eyes are not satisfied with riches; and [he says], For whom do I labor and take good from my soul? This [is] also vanity. Yes, it [is] an evil business.

title: Ecclesiastes 4:9
text: Two [are] better than one; because they have a good reward for their labor.

title: Ecclesiastes 4:10
text: For if they fall, the one will lift up his fellow; but woe to him [who is] alone when he falls, for he does not have another to help him.

title: Ecclesiastes 4:11
text: Again, if two lie [together], then they have warmth; but how can one be warm [alone]?

title: Ecclesiastes 4:12
text: And if one overthrows him, two shall withstand him; and a threefold cord is not quickly broken.

title: Ecclesiastes 4:13
text: A poor and a wise child [is] better than an old and foolish king, who will not be warned any more.

title: Ecclesiastes 4:14
text: For out of prison he comes to reign; although in his kingdom he was born poor.

title: Ecclesiastes 4:15
text: I saw all the living who walk under the sun, with the second child who shall stand up in his place.

title: Ecclesiastes 4:16
text: [There is] no end of all the people, of all who have been before them; they also who come after shall not rejoice in him. Surely this also [is] vanity and vexation of spirit.

title: Ecclesiastes 5:1
text: Guard your steps when you go to the house of God, and be more ready to hear than to give the sacrifice of fools. For they do not know that they are doing evil.

title: Ecclesiastes 5:2
text: Do not be rash [with] your mouth, and do not let your heart be hasty to say a word before God. For God [is] in Heaven, and you [are] on earth; therefore let your words be few.

title: Ecclesiastes 5:3
text: For a dream comes through the multitude of business; and a fool's voice by the multitude of words.

title: Ecclesiastes 5:4
text: When you vow a vow to God, do not wait to pay it. For He has no pleasure in fools. Pay that which you have vowed.

title: Ecclesiastes 5:5
text: [it is] better that you should not vow, than that you should vow and not pay.

title: Ecclesiastes 5:6
text: Do not allow your mouth to cause your flesh to sin; do not say before the angel that it [was] an error. Why should God be angry at your voice and destroy the work of your hands?

title: Ecclesiastes 5:7
text: For in the multitude of dreams, both words and vanities abound; but fear God.

title: Ecclesiastes 5:8
text: If you see the oppression of the poor, and violent perverting of judgment and justice in a province, do not marvel at the matter. For He [who is] higher than the highest watches; and there are some higher than they.

title: Ecclesiastes 5:9
text: And the advantage of a land, it is for all; [even] a king has a field being tilled.

title: Ecclesiastes 5:10
text: He who loves silver shall not be satisfied with silver, nor he who loves plenty does not gain. This [is] also vanity.

title: Ecclesiastes 5:11
text: When the good thing increases, those who eat it increase; then what profit [is it] to its owners, except to see [it] with their eyes?

title: Ecclesiastes 5:12
text: The sleep of a laboring man [is] sweet, whether he eats little or much; but the abundance of the rich will not allow him to sleep.

title: Ecclesiastes 5:13
text: There is a sore evil [which] I have seen under the sun, namely, riches kept for their owners to their hurt.

title: Ecclesiastes 5:14
text: But those riches perish by evil use. And he brings forth a son, and nothing [is] in his hand.

title: Ecclesiastes 5:15
text: As he came forth from his mother's womb naked, he shall return to go as he came. And from his labor he may not carry anything that may go in his hand.

title: Ecclesiastes 5:16
text: And this also [is] a sore evil, [that] in all, as he came, so shall he go; and what profit does he have who has labored for the wind?

title: Ecclesiastes 5:17
text: Also all his days he eats in darkness, and he has much sorrow and wrath [with] his sickness.

title: Ecclesiastes 5:18
text: Behold that which I have seen. [it is] good and right for one to eat and to drink, and to see good in all his labor that he labors under the sun all the days of his life, which God gives him; for it [is] his portion.

title: Ecclesiastes 5:19
text: Also every man to whom God has given riches and wealth, and has given him power to eat of it and to take his portion, and to rejoice in his labor this [is] the gift of God.

title: Ecclesiastes 5:20
text: For he shall not much remember the days of his life, because God answers [him] in the joy of his heart.

title: Ecclesiastes 6:1
text: There is an evil which I have seen under the sun, and it [is] great among men:

title: Ecclesiastes 6:2
text: a man to whom God has given riches, wealth, and honor, so that he lacks nothing for his soul of all that he desires, yet God does not give him power to eat of it, but a stranger eats it. This [is] vanity, and it [is] an evil disease.

title: Ecclesiastes 6:3
text: If a man fathers a hundred, and lives many years, so that the days of his years are many, and his soul is not filled with good, and also is for him no burial; I say, a miscarriage [is] better than he.

title: Ecclesiastes 6:4
text: For he comes in with vanity and goes out in darkness, and his name shall be covered with darkness.

title: Ecclesiastes 6:5
text: Also he has not seen the sun, nor known [anything]. This one has more rest than the other.

title: Ecclesiastes 6:6
text: Yea, though he live twice a thousand years, yet he has seen no good. Do not all go to one place?

title: Ecclesiastes 6:7
text: All the labor of man [is] for his mouth, and yet the appetite is not filled.

title: Ecclesiastes 6:8
text: For what [has] the wise more than the fool? What [gain has] the poor who knows [how] to walk before the living?

title: Ecclesiastes 6:9
text: Better [is] the sight of the eyes than the wandering of the desire. This [is] also vanity and vexation of spirit.

title: Ecclesiastes 6:10
text: That which has been [is] named already, and it is known that he [is] man. And he is not able to contend with Him who is mightier than he.

title: Ecclesiastes 6:11
text: For there are many things that increase vanity, [and] what [is] man the better?

title: Ecclesiastes 6:12
text: For who knows what [is] good for man in life, all the days of his vain life which he spends as a shadow? For who can tell a man what shall be after him under the sun?

title: Ecclesiastes 7:1
text: A good name [is] better than precious ointment, and the day of death than the day of one's birth.

title: Ecclesiastes 7:2
text: [It is] better to go to the house of mourning than to go to the house of feasting; for that [is] the end of all men; and the living will lay [it] to his heart.

title: Ecclesiastes 7:3
text: Sorrow [is] better than laughter; for by the sadness of the face the heart is made better.

title: Ecclesiastes 7:4
text: The heart of the wise [is] in the house of mourning; but the heart of fools [is] in the house of laughter.
